title: Social acceptance of a green ammonia hub in a remote coastal community – the case of Ísafjörður in Iceland
abstract: The International Maritime Organisation targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from international shipping by 2050, considering green ammonia to be a promising fuel for decarbonisation. However, development and deployment of this fuel is contingent not only on aspects such as techno-economic feasibility and supportive policy frameworks, but also on social acceptance (SA). This study examines the community-level SA of a potential green ammonia hub for maritime uses in Ísafjörður, Iceland, a remote coastal settlement with a strong maritime history. Based on sixteen semi-structured interviews with local stakeholders, the study identifies the key drivers and barriers influencing SA. It reveals that perceived benefits such as job creation and environmental protection function as drivers, while barriers stem from perceived concerns regarding safety, cost, and lack of clear governance. Guided by a community-adapted corporate sustainability classification and a PESTLE lens, identified themes are mapped across political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental dimensions. The findings indicate that political and governance conditions function as an important enabling condition for SA, particularly through the perceived need for clear legislative frameworks and government incentives. Rather than operating independently, these political conditions were closely intertwined with economic and technological considerations, influencing investment risk, infrastructure development, affordability, safety, and equitable benefit distribution. The study concludes that for a just maritime energy transition to succeed, national policymakers must prioritise the implementation of robust incentive mechanisms and strategic roadmaps that satisfactorily address local socio-economic realities and contexts.

title: Synergistic Interactions Enable Superior Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity in Compositionally Complex Nanocrystal–Nanosheet Hybrids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thiospinel nanoparticles are promising catalytic materials due to their compositional tunability, electronic conductivity, and structural stability. While significant gains in catalysis have been made through material engineering, one continuously developing route is through the use of support materials to enhance performance. Here, we report a simple, scalable, low-temperature method to coproduce colloidal multimetal nanocrystals (<20 nm in diameter) and In2S3-based nanosheets (<1 nm thick), forming compositionally complex hybrid nanocrystal–nanosheet heterostructures in situ. The in situ-formed heterostructures demonstrate enhanced catalytic activity in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in alkaline conditions; peak performance was achieved in heterostructures formed between (Ni,Co,Fe)3S4 nanocrystals and (In,Fe,Mn)2S3 nanosheets with overpotentials as low as 283 mV at 10 mA/cm2. Heterostructures can also be produced ex situ by introducing nanosheets, postsynthetically, to the nanocrystals, reducing the overpotential of (Ni,Co,Fe)3S4 nanocrystals from 362 mV to 312 mV with only a 5 wt % addition. This improvement highlights synergistic interactions in the heterostructures. These results suggest that an optimum nanosheet loading that maximizes effective nanocrystal–nanosheet interfacial coupling while preserving access to the Ni/Co-rich catalytic domains is the relevant design parameter. Our findings provide a low-temperature, colloidal route for synthesizing compositionally complex and highly uniform (<15% dispersity) sulfide nanocrystals, nanosheets, or heterostructures of the two with tunable structures and enhanced electrocatalytic performance. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a compositionally complex hybrid material that is able to enhance performance when formed both in situ or ex situ and the use of In2S3 as a scaffold for a support material for enhancing OER performance.

title: Zeolite-Confined Triatomic Cu Oxides at Silanol Nests as Hydrogen Transport Channels for H2 Production from Methanol Steam Reforming
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cu-based catalysts offer high methanol steam reforming (MSR) activity but are limited by unstable Cu+–Cu0 interconversions due to the redox and sintering labilities of Cu. Herein, we developed a universal amino-functionalized “gripper” strategy for firmly and precisely anchoring atomically dispersed metals (e.g., Cu, Co, Ni) within Beta-zeolite. Triatomic Cu oxide (Cu3Ox) sites lower the methanol dehydrogenation activation barrier, and the synergistic interplay with adjacent OH groups from silanol nests accelerates H2 evolution and the MSR reaction. Spatially decoupling Cu-mediated methanol activation from silanol-driven H2 evolution at silanol nests as proton transport channels within the confining zeolite framework also effectively protected Cu from sintering, achieving a high specific activity of 951 molH2·molCu–1·h–1 and over 600 h of stability under continuous regeneration. This work provides a universal strategy for synthesizing atomically dispersed metal catalysts and a new design principle for maintaining the Cu structure during MSR.

title: Tailoring Three-Dimensional Porphyrin Hosts to Control Fullerene Recognition and Charge-Separation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Porphyrin–fullerene assemblies are widely regarded as model systems in artificial photosynthesis. However, attaining precise structural control over both fullerene binding and charge-separation behavior within a single, rigid three-dimensional porphyrin host continues to be a significant challenge in supramolecular design. Dihydroanthracene- and triptycene-functionalized tetraarylporphyrins are shown here to act as biconcave aromatic hosts for C60, forming 1:1 and 1:2 complexes with association constants up to 104 to 105 M–1, as evidenced by 1H NMR and fluorescence titrations, and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry. Key in the host design is the porphyrin β,β-substitution that generates a well-defined and encapsulating environment for C60. Triptycenoporphyrins exhibit more geometrically confined C60 binding than their dihydroanthracene analogues, highlighting the critical role of topological control in C60 recognition. Despite identical binding strengths in nonpolar toluene and polar benzonitrile, the corresponding C60@triptycenoporphyrins display pronounced solvent-dependent excited-state behavior. Charge-separated states are generated more rapidly in benzonitrile yet attain significantly longer lifetimes in toluene, as revealed by steady-state and time-resolved spectroscopic measurements. These results demonstrate that tailoring rigid three-dimensional porphyrin frameworks enables simultaneous enhancement of C60 binding and fine control over charge-separation and -recombination dynamics, establishing this scaffold as a versatile platform for artificial photosynthetic systems that require long-lived charge-separation.

title: An Experimental MOF-Polymer Latent Space for Composite Design
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have tremendous promise for filtration, catalysis, and sequestration, but they are limited by the polymer matrices in which they must be embedded to form functional composites. Here, we find an experimental approach in which composite performance can be predicted using a single MOF particle. In particular, we attach single MOF particles to atomic force microscope (AFM) probes and find that the forces between the MOF-tipped probe and polymer films can be transformed into an instructive low-dimensional descriptor of MOF-polymer interactions. This two-dimensional latent space provides direct measures of chemical compatibility as well as the work of adhesion and can be used to understand interfacial phenomena in MOF-polymer composites. For example, polymer intercalation is observed via X-ray scattering for MOF-polymer combinations with high chemical-compatibility latent-space variables. Bulk composite performance can also be predicted using the latent space values for cases where the MOF is held constant. For example, a simple linear model was trained to predict CO2 absorption into composites of UiO-66-NH2 based solely on the latent space variables. In addition to providing a rapid way to screen polymer matrices to complement a MOF chosen for its bulk properties, these results suggest that composite performance may be a separable function of bulk properties and the interfacial latent space. In this way, this transfer-learning approach can vastly accelerate the design and understanding of functional composites.

title: Enantioselective Three-Component Reductive Coupling of Aldehydes, Amines, and Alkynes via Ligand-Enabled Cobalt/Photoredox Dual Catalysis for Modular Synthesis of Allylic Amines
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Here, we disclose a catalytic strategy that merges visible-light photoredox with cobalt catalysis to realize a previously elusive three-component enantioselective reductive coupling of readily available aldehydes, amines, and alkynes. This transformation provides a direct, step-economical route to high-value chiral allylic amines with broad substrate scope and high chemo-, regio-, and enantioselectivity, while overcoming long-standing challenges, including parasitic single-electron over-reduction, competitive aldehyde–alkyne coupling, and the inherent regioselectivity issues of unsymmetrical internal alkynes, and circumventing the moisture sensitivity and limited scope of pre-isolated imines. Central to this breakthrough is the rational design of a chiral phosphoramidite ligand featuring a tricyclic tetrahydrobenzoquinoline core, which avoids coordination saturation at cobalt and establishes a unique electronic “push–pull” synergy with a coordinated iodide anion. Mechanistic studies support an anion-promoted, single-ligand catalytic model wherein a high-spin cobaltacyclopentene intermediate serves as the key stereocontrol element. The monodentate, π-accepting phosphoramidite functions as a flexible electronic buffer, mitigating Pauli repulsion and dramatically lowering the oxidative cyclization barrier. The synthetic utility is demonstrated by late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules and a concise synthesis of the antiplatelet drug prasugrel.

title: Effect of Water on Elementary Reactions in Solid-Acid Catalyzed Reactions: Thermodynamics of Acid–Base Interactions in H-ZSM-5
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The influence of water on acid–base interactions in zeolites was quantified by measuring the enthalpy of pyridine adsorption on H-ZSM-5 with three Si/Al ratios (11.5, 40, and 140) in water using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). This calorimetric study reconciles the liquid- and gas-phase energetics of acid–base interactions in a solvated, pore-filled zeolite through a Born–Haber cycle analysis. In water, the apparent adsorption enthalpy is about 150 kJ/mol less exothermic than the gas-phase value and becomes more exothermic as the Si/Al ratio increases, whereas the gas-phase enthalpy is near −200 kJ/mol and independent of the Si/Al ratio. Since the intrinsic acid strength of the framework does not vary with Si/Al ratio, this increasing apparent adsorption energy trend with increasing Si/Al ratio reflects the influence of solvation rather than acidity. Water stabilizes both the acidic proton and the pyridinium ion, and a fraction of this stabilization is lost when adsorbed pyridine displaces water from the acid site. By combining ITC data with vapor-phase water adsorption isotherms and differential scanning calorimetry to construct a Born–Haber cycle for each zeolite, the aqueous-phase enthalpies are quantitatively reconciled with their gas-phase counterparts, and their dependence on Si/Al ratio is traced to the different extents to which the initial and final states are solvated.

title: Unifying Polar and Hydrophobic Models of Ice Recognition by Antifreeze Glycoproteins
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Antifreeze glycoproteins (AFGPs) enable polar organisms to survive at subzero temperatures by inhibiting ice growth through selective association with specific crystallographic planes. However, the molecular basis of this interaction and its remarkable selectivity remain incompletely understood, and both polar and hydrophobic binding models have been proposed. Here, we combine the synthesis of AFGP variants with high-resolution NMR spectroscopy, antifreeze activity measurements, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the molecular determinants of ice recognition. Minimally perturbative chemical modifications, including site-specific deuteration and fluorination, were used to probe the contributions of nonpolar and polar interactions while preserving the characteristic AFGP conformation. The combined structure–activity relationships and computational analyses support an integrative binding model that provides a unified and parsimonious interpretation of the experimental observations. Within this framework, our experimental evidence is consistent with the view that dispersive interactions involving peptide and carbohydrate methyl groups favor productive association with the ice surface, whereas carbohydrate hydroxyl groups, together with sugar- and backbone-associated water molecules, contribute polar interactions that promote selective and persistent binding. This model reconciles key aspects of previously proposed polar and hydrophobic descriptions and provides a molecular rationale for the characteristic plane selectivity of AFGPs and the conservation of specific sequence motifs. More broadly, our results highlight minimally perturbative isotopic substitution and fluorinated molecular editing as useful chemical strategies for probing weak dispersive contributions to complex molecular recognition processes while preserving native molecular architecture.

title: Evolution of Interfacial States Induced by Hydronium–Water Ordering on Au(111)
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Structured interfacial water can substantially modify charge transfer at solid–liquid interfaces, yet direct spectroscopic evidence for how water ordering reshapes interfacial electronic states remains scarce. Herein, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), we identify parabolic interfacial states (IFSs) arising with the ordered water structures on Au(111), in striking contrast to the insulating nature of disordered water multilayers. Light exposure induces partial dissociation of H2O, and the resulting hydrated protons combine with residual H2O molecules to form ordered Eigen/Zundel-type hexagonal hydronium-water monolayers on Au(111) at 120–140 K. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations based on Eigen/Zundel-type motifs reproduce the experimentally observed IFSs and indicate that the states derive from the renormalized Au(111) Shockley surface state with a reduced effective mass at the water/gold interface. Annealing-driven transition from the Eigen-type to Zundel-type monolayers is evidenced by the distinct changes in the dispersions of the IFSs. These results establish a band-structure perspective for ordered water/metal interfaces and show that hydrated-proton-introduced excess electrons, when confined at a two-dimensional interface, can reshape the interfacial electronic landscape and charge transport.

title: Magneto-Optical Studies on the Orbital Angular Momenta and Spin–Orbit Coupling in the Excited Triplet States of Octahedral Mo6 Clusters: Magnetic Circular Dichroism and Magnetic Circularly Polarized Luminescence
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The magneto-optical properties─magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) and magnetic circularly polarized luminescence (MCPL)─of octahedral hexanuclear [Mo6I8Y6]2– clusters (1, 2, and 3, possessing OPOPh2, N3, and CF3COO as the terminal Y ligands, respectively) were studied. In their MCD spectra, negative Faraday A terms corresponding to the S0 → Sn transitions were observed at ∼400 nm, reflecting the orbital angular momentum (OAM) and high symmetry of the molecular orbitals (MOs). In their highly concentrated solutions, positive Faraday A terms corresponding to the spin-forbidden S0 → Tn transitions were observed at ∼600 nm due to large spin–orbit coupling (SOC). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first direct observation of the spin-forbidden S0 → Tn transition in metal clusters by MCD. In their MCPL spectra, negative, strong phosphorescent MCPL signals (g ≈ 1.0 × 10–2 at 1.6 T) were observed at ∼690 nm, indicating that these Mo clusters are promising candidates for novel CPL materials. Time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations performed for the model cluster [Mo6I8Cl6]2– could reproduce UV–vis absorption and MCD spectroscopic properties. Especially, the MCD signals were evaluated by analyzing the SOC and the Zeeman effects of the OAM and spin angular momentum in the excited triplet state. TD-DFT gradient calculations indicated the geometrical distortion and stabilization of the lowest excited triplet [Mo6I8Cl6]2– and the destabilization of its Franck–Condon ground state, which explain the large red shift of phosphorescence. These results open new possibilities for understanding and functionalizing metal clusters.

title: Decyanation, Dioxygenation, and Oxidative Ring Contraction Catalyzed by the DUF4243 Oxidase OzmD Rely on Ferric Oxygen Activation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Domain of unknown function 4243 (DUF4243) family proteins are an emerging class of nonheme mononuclear iron enzymes characterized by a distinctive iron-binding motif comprised of four histidine (His) and one Nε-carboxylysine (Kcx) residue. Although predominantly found in fungi, OzmD is the only characterized bacterial member. OzmD catalyzes oxidative rearrangement of an aminopyridone ring into a 1,3-oxazine moiety with concomitant cyanide elimination in the final step of oxazinomycin biosynthesis. Herein, the X-ray crystal structure of OzmD is solved, demonstrating the presence of a conserved 4-His-1-Kcx iron-binding motif similar to other DUF4243 family proteins. Biochemical characterization using a substrate analog carrying a hydroxypyridone ring reveals that OzmD also exhibits intrinsic dioxygenase activity, catalyzing a transformation analogous to those of fungal DUF4243 dioxygenases. Electron paramagnetic resonance and Mössbauer spectroscopic characterization of MinCC, a functionally equivalent homologue of OzmD, reveals that the as-isolated protein predominantly contains ferric iron, which can be reduced to the ferrous state upon binding with either the native substrate or the hydroxy analog under anaerobic conditions. These findings support a unified mechanism in which catalysis begins with single-electron transfer from the substrate to ferric iron, enabling molecular oxygen activation and formation of an alkylperoxide intermediate. Overall reaction mechanisms for substrates bearing aminopyridone and hydroxypyridone rings are proposed based on chemical precedents and computational analyses. These findings reveal that OzmD employs a distinctive FeIII-dependent path for oxygen activation in contrast to the classical FeII-dependent route used by most oxygenases and establish a functional connection between bacterial and fungal DUF4243 enzymes.

title: Optical Access to a Molecular Nuclear-Spin Register in Catalytically Relevant Palladium(I) Complexes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Paramagnetic metal complexes are powerful tools in chemical catalysis and, increasingly, quantum information science, positioning them as ideal tools for quantum sensing within reactions themselves. However, this application requires an interface between spins and light in chemically relevant platforms. Here, we demonstrate that circularly polarized light can generate electron spin coherence in low-symmetry, catalytically relevant Pd(I) complexes. By measuring ultrafast changes in optical polarization with time-resolved Faraday rotation, we optically detect coherent superhyperfine interaction between the Pd(I)-centered electron spin and adjacent 31P nuclei from the ligand at ambient temperature in solution. The electronic origins of this behavior are attributed to excited-state orbital angular momentum through combined spectroscopic and computational analysis, and the optically measured coherence is benchmarked against pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance. Spin polarization is coherently exchanged between the electron spin and initially incoherent nuclear spins, constituting a rare example of optical access to a nuclear spin register in an ambient-temperature, solution-phase molecular system. Both reactivity and quantum spin function are mediated by the bisphosphine ligand; taken together with in situ detection of coherent Pd(I) spin dynamics directly in reaction mixtures, this work moves molecular qubits toward quantum sensing in chemical reactions.

title: Mechanism-Guided Development of Thioacetylene Probes for Chemoproteomic Profiling of Cellular Protein Thiyl Radicals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Protein thiyl radicals are transient reactive intermediates involved in oxidative stress and enzymatic catalysis. However, their proteome-wide, site-resolved profiling in living cells remains challenging due to the lack of suitable tools. Here, we report chemoproteomic probes enabling covalent capture and site-resolved identification of protein thiyl radicals in living cells. Designed to leverage sulfur-mediated stabilization of a vinyl radical intermediate, our thioacetylene-based probes selectively capture cysteine thiyl radicals while minimizing cross-reactivity with nucleophilic thiolates and nonradical amino acid residues. In vitro validation and live-cell chemoproteomic analysis established radical-dependent labeling and site-resolved detection of protein thiyl radicals. Notably, the probes enabled site-specific mapping of thiyl radical-associated cysteine residues in live E. coli, including Cys439 of ribonucleotide reductase A (NrdA), a canonical enzymatic thiyl radical site. Expanded residue profiling further confirmed cysteine-predominant labeling and detected probe modification at established and putative glycyl radical residues in PflB, NrdD, and YjjI, suggesting that the platform may extend beyond thiyl radicals to other protein-centered radicals. Application of the probe under oxidative and nitrosative stress revealed condition-dependent changes in cellular protein radical-associated labeling, including decreased labeling at established glycyl radical residues and bidirectional changes in cysteine radical-associated labeling. Together, these findings establish thioacetylene probes as a platform for site-resolved mapping and comparative monitoring of endogenous protein-centered radicals in living cells.

title: Dynamic Nonlinear Effects in the Asymmetric Kinetic Resolution Polymerization of Racemic Diazoacetates to One-Handed Helical Polycarbenes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The asymmetric kinetic resolution polymerization (AKRP) of racemic diazoacetates mediated by a [Rh(cod)Cl]2/chiral amine dual catalyst system exhibits dynamic nonlinear effects (DNLEs) in the relative rate constant (Krel). The overall Krel increases nonlinearly with the monomer conversion during polymer chain propagation and reaches a plateau at a medium conversion. These DNLEs originate from synergistic chirality amplification between the catalytic chain end and the evolving helical conformation of the growing polymer chain. Under optimized conditions, Krel increases from 15 at 3% monomer conversion to ∼ 138 at 33% conversion, and then reaches a plateau. The steric bulk of both the pendant groups of monomers and the chiral amine ligand critically regulates the magnitude and evolution of DNLEs, and reducing this bulk leads to a pronounced decrease in Krel. Chain extension experiments using the preformed helical macroinitiators exhibited a constant Krel, confirming that a well-formed helical conformation maintains stable enantioselectivity for AKRP. Computational studies further revealed that, during chain propagation, decameric species with well-developed helical conformations exhibit more pronounced energy differences between the R- and S-enantiomers than the corresponding initial monomer-inserted species. These results suggest that the one-handed helical conformation is associated with the enhanced enantiomer recognition at the catalytic center. This study reveals DNLEs in AKRP in which enantioselectivity evolves nonlinearly during polymer chain propagation, highlighting a dynamic chiral amplification mechanism that can surpass the intrinsic selectivity of a static catalyst through the cooperative action of chiral chain ends and helical conformation.

title: Electronic Dynamics in Long Linear and Cyclic Polyynes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Carbyne─the one-dimensional sp-hybridized allotrope of carbon─has long been predicted to exhibit unique properties, yet its synthesis remains elusive. To probe its behavior, finite sp-carbon chains such as cumulenes and polyynes have been studied. While much has been established about the ground-state properties of cumulenes and polyynes, our understanding of their photophysical dynamics, which gives critical insight into how electronic relaxation, structural reorganization, and spin formation evolve, has focused almost exclusively on short, linear systems, with little consideration of topology. Here, we investigate long 48-carbon linear and cyclic polyynes in the liquid phase using steady-state and ultrafast, temperature- and polarization-resolved optical and vibrational spectroscopy. We find highly delocalized ground states in both topologies, with softened Peierls distortion and reduced bond-length alternation relative to shorter chains. In contrast, the excited state singlet dipole depolarization mechanism and subsequent intersystem crossing are strongly dependent on chain length and topology. As in shorter polyynes, transient infrared spectroscopy shows that photoexcitation of long linear polyynes induces a cumulene-like excited-state geometry; however, this structural rearrangement is weaker and shorter-lived than in shorter analogues. Comparison with shorter-chain trends and theoretical predictions shows that the Huang–Rhys factor remains far below the ideal infinite-chain value at 48 carbons, suggesting that vibronic coupling grows more slowly at long chain length than expected from simple extrapolation. Our results reveal how topology influences the largely backbone-dominated electronic dynamics of long polyynes and refine our understanding of finite sp-carbon systems at longer chain lengths than previously accessible with such time-resolved methods.

title: Non-local Molecular Engineering Modulates Aluminum-Induced Crystallization toward Transferable Polycrystalline Silicon
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Low-temperature metal-induced crystallization (MIC) has emerged as a promising and cost-effective technique for fabricating polycrystalline silicon (poly-Si), which is a key material in high-performance flexible electronics. However, conventional MIC often yields structurally compromised films due to chaotic interfacial thermodynamics and incomplete layer exchange. Herein, a molecular-level engineering strategy is presented that utilizes buried self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) to remotely control the macroscopic phase transformation and crystallization kinetics during MIC with aluminum as the metal. By systematically tailoring the terminal functional groups of the SAMs at the buried interface between the Al/Si stack and substrate (glass), a distinct structure-property relationship is established: electron-withdrawing groups intrinsically stabilize the amorphous Si (a-Si) network and suppress segregation, whereas electron-donating groups facilitate silicon dissolution. Notably, the best-performing SAM with nucleophilic –NH2 terminal groups functions as a dual-role molecular template that drastically lowers the macroscopic crystallization barrier of the MIC system. By driving a highly directed and accelerated kinetic pathway, this monolayer substantially suppresses stochastic interdiffusion, yielding a highly segregated, continuous, and transfer-ready poly-Si film. Ultimately, this SAM-mediated paradigm advances the fundamental design of non-local phase transformations, establishing a scalable, material-driven pathway for next-generation flexible silicon electronics.

title: Capacity design in district energy systems with thermal energy storage – a new planning paradigm
abstract: Planning future district energy systems is increasingly challenged by uncertainties in demand growth and spatial development. Conventional planning resolves this by oversizing infrastructure to meet projected peak demand – tying up capital in assets used a fraction of the year, with reactive upgrades required where demand develops beyond projections. The result is a persistent trade-off between cost, emissions, and resiliency. This study proposes a new paradigm for capacity design that treats thermal energy storage (TES) – and particularly strategically placed decentralized TES (DecTES) – as an integrated design element that adds a degree of freedom to the capacity design problem. While centralized TES reduces peak production requirements, DecTES additionally resolves transmission bottlenecks by absorbing peak demand locally, adding a spatial dimension to system flexibility. The approach is demonstrated on district cooling and heating systems at Stanford, California, and Aalborg, Denmark. At Stanford, existing TES reduces operational expenditures (OPEX) by ~12% and CO₂ emissions by ~7% annually; doubling TES potentially adds ~2% OPEX and ~1.5% CO₂ savings, and DecTES enables 20–23% local demand growth without infrastructure expansion. In Aalborg, existing TES delivers ~10% OPEX savings and ~17% CO₂ reductions; DecTES enables 20–28% local demand growth at baseline and 54–62% under adaptive operation, potentially adds ~2.5% OPEX and ~5% CO₂ savings, and phases out decentralized fossil peak production. Illustrative tests indicate electricity-grid benefits, with potential connection-capacity reductions of up to 25% and 53%. Unlike conventional peak capacity, TES delivers year-round value from day one – reducing planning risk regardless of how demand unfolds.

title: Bridge fuels and climate policy integration: The case of low-carbon hydrogen in the European Union
abstract: Hydrogen is central to climate neutrality in the European Union (EU), particularly in hard-to-abate sectors. The EU promotes fossil-based low-carbon hydrogen (LCH) as a bridge fuel supporting the development of a renewable hydrogen economy, despite risks of insufficient emission reductions and diverted investments. Climate policy integration (CPI) research has not addressed hydrogen and lacks a benchmark for bridge fuels. Earlier studies permitted a constrained role for natural gas, whereas recent work deems fossil fuels inherently incompatible with CPI, but without examining the transitional role of bridge fuels. Analyzing 182 legal acts and communications, this article provides the first systematic CPI assessment of the EU hydrogen framework. It provides a CPI benchmark for bridge fuels with three jointly necessary conditions (significant emission reductions, temporal limitation, support for target technologies), assessed through the thickness and quality of the policy mix across four indicators (policy goals, policy instruments for emission reductions, funding/financing, and procedural instruments). The hydrogen framework reaches a medium level of CPI. Its policy mix is thick but lacks quality, applying the conditions of bridge fuels only selectively. The framework thus commits neither to a net-zero pathway nor to an end date for fossil-based LCH. Conceptually, the article shows that the compatibility of fossil-based technologies with CPI depends on the climate policy paradigm underlying the benchmark. Under a purely emission-based decarbonization benchmark, they are not inherently incompatible with CPI. Where fossil-free alternatives exist, however, they should align with CPI only as temporally limited bridge fuels, following a defossilization paradigm.

title: Co-optimization of intraday and frequency containment reserve bids for battery energy storage
abstract: As renewable energy integration increases supply variability, battery energy storage systems (BESS) present a viable solution for balancing supply and demand. This paper proposes a joint bidding strategy that combines participation in the primary frequency reserve market with continuous trading in the intraday market, addressing a gap in the extant literature that typically considers these markets in isolation and simplifies the continuous nature of intraday trading. Our approach utilizes a mixed integer linear programming implementation of the rolling intrinsic algorithm for intraday decisions and state of charge recovery, alongside a learned classifier strategy (LCS) that determines optimal day-ahead capacity allocation between markets. A comprehensive out-of-sample backtest over more than one year of tick level historical German market data validates our approach: The LCS increases overall profits by over 4% compared to the best-performing static strategy and by more than 3% over a naive dynamic benchmark. Crucially, our method closes the gap to a theoretical perfect foresight strategy to just 4%, demonstrating the effectiveness of dynamic, learning-based allocation in a complex, multi-market environment.

title: Robust optical skyrmion arising from randomness
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Optical skyrmions, known as topological quasiparticles, have emerged as a distinct photonic degree of freedom with great potential and promising prospects for broad applications. Prior studies have predominantly focused on skyrmions in fully coherent light fields. In this paper, we show that incoherent optical skyrmions can arise from an ensemble of random modes whose statistical correlations are deliberately engineered. Under external obstacles, the engineered statistical correlations enable reconstruction of the focal field, while the skyrmion topology provides a quantized global measure of the structural robustness. Beyond enabling programmable control over skyrmion topology by tailoring these correlations, the statistical construction suppresses the fixed-phase interference between neighboring skyrmion units inherent in coherent superpositions. The demonstrated robustness under obstacles, enhanced skyrmion density resolution, and flexible generation of programmable arrays extensively expand the skyrmion family and offer insights into optical quasiparticles, with potential applications in photonics.

title: Designing additives for perovskite transistors using molecular polarity as a guide
abstract: Molecular polarity can be used as a predictive descriptor to screen potential additives for halide perovskite lattices, allowing robust and high-performance tin-based perovskite transistors to be created.

title: Impact of energetic alpha particles on core turbulence in an ARC-class fusion power plant
abstract: In this work, we investigate the impact of fusion-born alpha particles on core turbulence and transport in the ARC tokamak fusion power plant (Hillesheim et al 2026 J. Plasma Phys.92 E69) using linear and nonlinear gyrokinetic CGYRO (Candy et alJ. Comput. Phys.324 73–93) simulations. A significant reduction in ion-scale turbulent heat and particle fluxes is observed in the inner core (r/a 0.5), which is associated with multiscale interactions between fast ion-destabilized modes, zonal flows, and the background turbulence. A nonlinear upshift in the ITG critical gradient is observed in the simulations with fast alphas compared to those with artificially thermalized alphas. The turbulence reduction is found to scale beneficially with alpha particle density and plasma , and the radial extent of the turbulence suppression is limited to the volume containing a significant density of fast particles. The suitability of local gyrokinetics and potential impacts of fast ion effects on fusion performance are discussed.

title: Pellet induced transition from low to high confinement in separatrix phase spaces of ASDEX Upgrade
abstract: The Separatrix Operational Space (SepOS) concept (Eich and Manz 2021 Nucl. Fusion61 086017) describes the operational space of tokamaks with respect to MHD, density limits and the L-H transition in terms of density and temperature at the separatrix. It has been inspired by the phase space developed by Rogers et al (1998 Phys. Rev. Lett.81 4396) Rogers, Drake, and Zeiler (RDZ). Their idea was contested by pellet-induced L-H transitions (Gohil et al 2001 Phys. Rev. Lett.86 644) evaluated inside the pedestal and subsequently this theory was widely dismissed. Whether the SepOS concept face similar challenges when applied to a pellet-induced L-H transition is studied. On the low-density branch of the L-H transition, the separatrix density is temporarily increased by pellet injection, thereby lowering the L-H power threshold in agreement with the SepOS model. The results will also be discussed in RDZ’s phase space. We conclude that the basic idea of the plasma edge phase space proposed by RDZ, more precisely that an increase in plasma beta at low collisionalities has a beneficial effect on confinement and at high collisionalities has a detrimental effect on confinement, was discarded unjustly.

title: Switchable nucleophile-electrophile chemistry enables functional four-electron Li-I2 batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Four-electron iodine redox chemistry offers a high theoretical specific energy of ~1324 Wh kgI−1, yet its practical realization is fundamentally limited by the conflicting demands of rapid I0/I+ oxidation, effective suppression of iodine shuttling, and stabilization of highly reactive I+ species. Here we report a redox-active, Lewis acid/base-tunable phthalimide that resolves these constraints through a single-molecule polarity-switching mechanism. Upon electrochemical oxidation, electrophilic phthalimideδ+ strongly interacts with nucleophilic iodine and polyiodide species, concurrently suppressing polyiodide shuttling and promoting their conversion to I+. The consecutively generated phthalimideδ− acts as a nucleophilic stabilizer for the resulting I+ species. This electrochemically driven polarity switching of phthalimide enables flexible four-electron Li-I2 pouch cells that deliver ~400 mAh gI−1 capacity, a specific energy exceeding 1200 Wh kgI−1, a high cathode-level specific energy ( ~ 883.4 Wh kg(cathode)−1), and stable cycling over 1000 cycles. The successful integration of these cells into wearable wireless charging and motion-sensing systems demonstrates the potential of polarity-switchable iodine chemistry for next-generation flexible energy-storage devices.

title: Single photon reflection from a quantum dot in a waveguide
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Single-atom waveguide-QED systems have emerged as a leading platform for demonstrating non-linear optics in the few-photon regime. Devices with such non-linear behavior are necessary for developing deterministic gates for photonic quantum computing. Artificial atoms coupled to nanophotonic or superconducting waveguides can be used to engineer highly efficient light-matter interfaces for such non-linear interactions, where every photon in the system interacts with the quantum emitter. However, it has been a challenge to access the reflection port of the waveguide due to the inability of rejecting stray electromagnetic fields that do not interact with the artificial atom. Here, we show coherent reflection of single photons from a semiconductor quantum dot strongly coupled to the fundamental waveguide mode of a nanowire. We utilize the tapered end of the nanowire for ideal mode-matching in a vertical geometry, enabled by the extinction technique developed. This mode-matching allows for efficient transfer of photons from the input to the reflection port while having all interacted with the quantum dot. Such a high-efficiency scalable photonic platform opens up applications in few-photon quantum nonlinear optics and has been proposed for creating key resource states for universal photon-based quantum computing.

title: Low-thermal-budget solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric for low-voltage 2D electronics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Low-voltage and high-performance electronic devices based on two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors demand high-quality dielectrics with efficient capacitive gating. However, it currently relies on specially engineered atomic layer deposition (ALD) of ultrathin high-k HfO2 and ZrO2, or high-temperature vapor-phase growth of 2D dielectrics with post-growth transfer process. Here, we report a facile solution-processed 2D dielectric with an ultra-low thermal budget (i.e., at room temperature), while delivering competitive device metrics (e.g., low operating voltage and small hysteresis). This is enabled by an organic-free colloidal ink of montmorillonite (MTM) in environmentally friendly water solvent, eliminating the need for organic ligands or surfactants and thus the post-deposition high-temperature thermal annealing. Specifically, all-solution-processed MoS2 field-effect transistors with MTM dielectric exhibit a low operating voltage of 1 V and small hysteresis (down to 1 mV). The solution process is generally compatible with diverse n-type and p-type 2D semiconductors such as MoS2, MoSe2 and WSe2. Moreover, the robust and reproducible MTM dielectric enables scalable device integration into logic circuits, including inverters, AND, NOR, and NAND gates, as well as static random-access memory (SRAM). The scalable room-temperature solution-processed 2D dielectric offers a route to all-solution-processed and low-voltage 2D electronics.

title: High-pressure synthesis of a polymeric N3H2 solid stabilized by hydrogen bonds
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polymeric nitrogen represents a long-sought class of high energy density materials, in which single-bonded nitrogen networks release large amounts of energy upon decomposition to molecular N2. However, polymeric nitrogen allotropes require extreme pressures to synthesize and cannot be recovered at ambient conditions due to surface instabilities. Hydrogen has been proposed as a key element to stabilize such frameworks, yet polymeric nitrogen–hydrogen solids have until now remained the realm of theoretical calculations. Here, we report the high-pressure synthesis of polymeric N3H2 at 134(3)–139(1) GPa from N2–H2 mixtures. Synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy and first-principles calculations reveal a fully single-bonded framework of 1-dimensional chains of N6 rings, each decorated by four H atoms. The chains of N6H4 units are cross-linked through hydrogen bonds. Employing modern synchrotron sources, hydrogen positions are directly resolved from diffraction data at 139(1) GPa. At ambient conditions, N3H2 exhibits an estimated energy of decomposition of 7.98 kJ/g, highlighting hydrogen-stabilized polymeric nitrogen as a promising class of energetic materials.

title: Geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive COFs for selective recognition of multiple uranium species in complex waters
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sustainable uranium supply is critical for nuclear energy, yet its practical recovery is severely hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium in natural waters. In dynamic aqueous environments, uranium continuously shifts between large, cationic hydrolyzed clusters (acidic/neutral) and compact, anionic carbonate complexes (alkaline). Conventional static adsorbents fail to accommodate these contrasting charges and geometries. Here, we report a geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive three-dimensional covalent organic framework (COF), TAM-DTDA-AMM, to overcome this speciation barrier. Featuring a three-fold interpenetrated dia topology, the functional COF enables environment-driven reversible −COO−···NH4+ ion-pair reconfiguration, coupling adaptive pore-surface chemistry with dynamic spatial confinement. Under alkaline environments, cationic microdomains stabilize [UO2(CO3)3]4− via electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions, whereas under near-neutral to acidic conditions, protonated carboxyl groups directly coordinate hydrolyzed uranyl clusters. This dual-adaptive mechanism enables rapid, selective, and high-capacity uranium extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries and offers a general strategy for recognizing multiple metal species in complex environments.

title: Activation of high-lying dormant states by cascaded transition control in core@shell upconversion nanoparticles
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lanthanide-doped upconversion nanoparticles exhibit multicolor emission through discrete, narrowband transitions, enabling applications in bioimaging, lasers, and displays. However, the trade-off between leveraging abundant energy levels for multicolor output and mitigating rapid deactivation of high-lying states remains a fundamental challenge for achieving balanced white-light emission under moderate excitation power. This is particularly true for emitters such as Ho3+, which are highly susceptible to severe multiphonon relaxation and back energy transfer. Here, we address this by introducing a core@shell cascaded transition strategy that selectively populates Ho3+ high-lying states via engineered energy relays at a key intermediate level, Ce3+-mediated cross-relaxation control, and precise spatial ion arrangement. Our design achieves a ∼1500-fold boost in blue emission versus conventional architectures, enabling balanced red, green and blue output at 10 W/cm2 (10 mg/mL suspension). This white-light system surpasses mixed-nanoparticle media in stability, producing white lasers for photonics. Our approach provides a versatile route to high-lying states activation in lanthanide systems, with potential implications for multicolor imaging, displays, and anti-counterfeiting.

title: Climate-driven screening maps and design rules for PCM-assisted cooling of photovoltaic modules
Critical raw material intensity of electricity generation technologies: A probabilistic and multicriteria approach applied to the European Union
abstract: The global energy transition is expected to substantially increase the deployment of renewable electricity technologies in the European Union (EU), intensifying both consumption and dependency on critical raw materials. Existing studies do not support robust comparisons between electricity generation technologies for decision-making in energy planning and policy. In this context, the present study proposes a probabilistic multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) framework to assess and rank electricity generation technologies according to their material requirements in t/MWh. It incorporates at least one method from each major MADM family and includes strategies to enhance resilience against rank reversal. Material consumptions are aggregated into satisfaction or criticality indices, while Monte Carlo simulation captures uncertainty and variability in consumption, lifetimes, and operational conditions. The methodology is applied to the EU including eight electricity generation technologies (wind, solar PV, solar CSP, hydro, biomass and waste, nuclear, coal, and natural gas) and 33 raw materials. Despite minor differences among MADM methods, the framework consistently converges on a ranking in which wind and solar PV are the most material-critical technologies, followed by solar CSP; coal, natural gas and nuclear occupy intermediate positions; biomass and waste, and hydro are the least critical alternatives. These findings highlight that EU decarbonisation strategies must be complemented by targeted raw material policies, including diversification of supply, recycling, material substitution, and strategic planning, to ensure that the transition to renewable electricity is not only low-carbon but also materially resilient and secure.

Probing topological edge states in a molecular synthetic dimension
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Synthetic dimensions, where additional spatial dimensions are encoded within the internal states of a quantum system, allow the realisation of phenomena usually inaccessible in experiments. Ultracold polar molecules are an ideal platform for synthetic dimensions, providing large Hilbert spaces of long-lived rotational and hyperfine states that can be linked with microwave fields to simulate tunnelling. Here, we realise a one-dimensional synthetic lattice using the rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules and investigate the topological properties of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. We spectroscopically probe the system using an auxiliary rotational state and study the time dynamics after deterministic state preparation. We demonstrate long coherence times, reaching ~ 500 tunnelling periods even for lattices spanning eight rotational states. Using full site-resolved readout over long evolution times, we study the robustness of topologically protected edge states against perturbations that preserve or break chiral symmetry. These results establish ultracold molecules as a powerful platform for quantum simulation using synthetic dimensions.

title: Topographical mismatch sustains open microchannels in living soft tissue for non-destructive protein biopsy
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sustaining open microchannels within living soft tissue has remained a problem of mechanics: implants rigid enough to maintain patent channels inflict inflammation, while implants compliant enough to avoid it are sealed within minutes by viscoelastic recoil. Here, we resolve this conflict through topographical mismatch—a deliberate geometric non-conformity between an ultrathin multi-lobed implant and the surrounding tissue. Engineered to exceed the conformability limit of skin, these conduits sustain patency for over 42 hours of sustained physiological deformation and for at least 7 days in living skin without triggering the mechanotransductive signalling that initiates fibrotic encapsulation, and transmit macromolecules of up to 70 kilodaltons through intact skin—surpassing the molecular weight ceiling of transdermal iontophoresis. In vivo, this access reveals that interstitial fluid concentration of a model protein peaks 4.7-fold higher than serum at 2 hours, inverts at 8 hours and rebounds by 24 hours, uncovering tissue-level pharmacokinetics inaccessible to blood sampling. Topographical mismatch establishes a generalisable design principle for sustained, biocompatible interfaces between soft devices and living tissue.

title: Frequency-constrained robust unit commitment for an integrated electricity-heat system considering heterogeneous resources

Ferrocene heteroconjugation enables charge transport in DNA monolayers
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: DNA has emerged as a promising self-assembling material for molecular electronics. Here, we investigate the electrical response of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) modified with a ferrocene-functionalised psoralen that forms a covalent cross-link at TA–AT sites. A thiol-modified 10-mer DNA conjugate self-assembles on Au substrates, enabling simultaneous mapping of surface topography and current distribution by conductive atomic force microscopy. Under the present experimental conditions, native dsDNA remained close to the current detection limit, whereas incorporation of ferrocene resulted in a measurable increase. Analysis of the current–voltage characteristics did not reveal a clear signature of a single dominant transport mechanism. At higher fields, the response was consistent with field-assisted charge injection across the molecular junction. These results indicate that ferrocene incorporation modifies the electronic response of the DNA assembly and influences charge transport across the molecular layer. This approach requires no pre-derivatisation of the DNA backbone and provides a versatile strategy for post-synthetic functionalisation.

title: DLS-Extended: a reduced model to assess the impact of impurity radiation location on optimal magnetic geometry choices for the STEP divertor
abstract: Alternative Divertor Configurations (ADCs) often make use of high total flux expansion ( ) and connection length ( ) to improve the access to and the controllability of detachment, a regime vitally important for reactor-class tokamaks such as the Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production (STEP). Achieving detachment on such high-power devices is enabled through radiation from seeded impurity species such as argon and neon, which can lead to radiative losses throughout the flux tube, altering the impact of magnetic geometry on detachment. The detachment location sensitivity (DLS) model analytically predicts detachment access and sensitivity based on upstream conditions, the magnetic geometry and seeded impurity radiation. It assumes the radiation region to have no spatial extent. In this work, we relax this assumption and introduce DLS-Extended, a new reduced 1D model which can capture the effects of the spatial distribution of impurity radiation along the field line. The prediction of radiation extent was verified against SOLPS-ITER simulations of an initial STEP design with a good match. DLS-Extended predicts that the radiation extent found in STEP weakens the detachment access benefit of and strengthens the benefit of , while the detachment stability of the inner and outer legs is increased and decreased, respectively. This is due to a number of novel radiation-driven effects and has implications for the optimum strike point position in reactor-scale devices. These findings highlight the need for more experimental studies in the presence of broad-radiating impurities. DLS-Extended is distributed under the LGPL-3 open source license and is publicly available on GitHub.

title: All-Visible Wavelength-Gated Multistate Photochromic AIEgen: High-Efficiency Photocyclizations in a Single Luminogenic System
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Synthetic photochromic molecules that enable noninvasive orthogonal control using distinct wavelengths of light are still in their infancy, yet ensuring the independence of photoreaction pathways and multiple addressable states in a single luminogenic system remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) luminogen capable of undergoing wavelength-selective photocyclizations under visible-light irradiation, exhibiting a photorearrangement at 410 nm purple light and an oxidative photocyclization at 465 nm blue light to yield two stable yet distinct photochromic states. Experimental and theoretical results provide insight into the wavelength-dependent reaction pathways, as well as the corresponding synergistic mechanism of aromaticity, steric strain, and inductive effect in its photocyclizations. Eventually, a model information encryption system was developed to showcase its practical potential for all-visible-light-controlled multistate operations. This work thus offers both a viable strategy and a versatile structural motif for developing visible-light-controlled multistate luminogens and advanced multifunctional systems.

abstract: Molecular polarity can be used to guide the rational and targeted design of additives that suppress ion migration in metal halide perovskite transistors, leading to mobilities of over 40 cm2 V−1 s−1 and stabilities of over 9,000 on/off cycles.

title: Distributionally robust bidding of a hybrid high-temperature thermal and compressed air energy storage system in power markets under wind power uncertainty
abstract: Compressed Air Energy Storage is a large-scale energy storage technology capable of participating in power markets while being integrated with power systems to facilitate higher levels of wind power integration. This paper investigates the potential of a new hybrid High-temperature thermal and Compressed Air Energy Storage (Hi-CAES) system to participate in energy and reserve markets to present its commercial value while supporting power system operation and wind power integration. A bidding model is proposed and formulated as a bi-level distributionally robust optimisation (DRO) problem. The upper-level problem aims to maximise Hi-CAES's financial gains through strategic bidding, while the lower-level problem models the energy and reserve markets clearing as well as power system scheduling subject to the integration of variable wind power. A multi-stage Wasserstein DRO method is developed to capture the non-anticipative wind uncertainty during the scheduling process. In addition, the bidding model incorporates a novel adaptive reserve requirement (ARR) mechanism, which adaptively sets reserve requirements for market participants to maintain system power balance under wind power uncertainty. Case studies on the UK regional 45-bus system validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and demonstrate the operational and economic advantages of the Hi-CAES system and ARR mechanism.

title: Optimal co-planning of hybrid energy hubs and integrated electricity-hydrogen transmission infrastructure
abstract: Clusters of large-scale renewable energy projects, also known as renewable energy zones (REZs), are essential elements in the transition to net zero. Hybrid energy hubs (HEHs), which incorporate other energy vectors such as green hydrogen (H 2 ) into REZs, can further leverage economies of scale and diversity in electricity and H 2 production and demand to reduce the required capacity of connection assets and decrease overall operational and capital costs. This paper introduces a general, optimization-based framework for the co-planning of HEHs and integrated electricity and H 2 systems (IEHS), aiming to find the least-cost designs of HEHs, along with the electricity and H 2 transmission infrastructure required to connect them to the main grid. This framework features a modular HEH model that enables flexible technology selection and sizing without a predefined hub configuration, while minimizing the capacity of shared connection assets. Comprehensive case studies on the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM) that integrate HEH and system-level planning compare investment strategies between independent connection configurations and shared connection configurations within HEHs. The findings show that integrating HEHs with optimized shared connection assets into IEHS planning can not only displace investments in both electricity and H 2 transmission infrastructure, but also reduce renewable energy curtailment and enhance the utilization of existing and new assets. Moreover, although including H 2 transmission development can reduce system costs, HEHs with shared connection assets alone may provide greater cost reductions as an alternative investment strategy, enough to avoid all the uncertainty associated with building a new H 2 pipeline network.

title: Zero-excess sodium-metal batteries for post-lithium energy storage
abstract: Zero-excess sodium-metal batteries combine high energy density, resource abundance and simplified manufacturing, positioning them as a potential post-lithium energy-storage technology. This Review examines the promise of this technology, the failure mechanisms and design principles of zero-excess sodium-metal batteries, and their deployment readiness.

title: Room-temperature fabrication of 2D nanomaterials
abstract: Two-dimensional nanomaterials are usually made at high temperatures, which is costly and hard to scale up. This review compares room-temperature exfoliation methods that peel layered crystals into ultrathin sheets, examining their yields, defect levels, and flake sizes. It proposes reporting standards and a decision flowchart to help researchers choose the right method for a given application and highlights hybrid processes, real-time monitoring, and AI-driven optimization as promising routes toward industrial production.

title: Near-infrared plasmonic response in hyperdoped silicon nanoantennas for all-silicon photodetection
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Plasmonic materials enable subwavelength confinement of light through the collective response of free carriers, but their operational spectral range is typically constrained by intrinsic carrier densities. Hyperdoped semiconductors offer a route to engineer plasmonic properties within a CMOS-compatible platform, yet their plasmonic response in silicon remains largely limited to the mid-infrared. Here we show that nanoantenna engineering extends the plasmonic response of phosphorus-hyperdoped silicon toward the near-infrared. The nanoantenna arrays exhibit tunable, polarization-dependent resonances in the 1–2 μm range, arising from geometry-driven localized modes on a Drude-like electronic background. Leveraging these effects, we realize all-silicon photoconductive detectors operating at 1.55 μm and room temperature, with a maximum bias-assisted responsivity of 0.58 A/W at 0.5 V. This response arises from plasmon-enhanced sub-bandgap absorption combined with trap-assisted photoconductive gain and therefore does not represent the intrinsic quantum efficiency. These results extend the spectral functionality of silicon photonics beyond its intrinsic absorption limits for integrated sensing, imaging, and optical communication.

title: Toward triggered generation of indistinguishable single photons from MoTe2 quantum emitters
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Single-photon sources operating at telecom wavelengths are fundamental components for long-distance optical quantum communication and information processing. Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides offer a promising platform for such sources, but their development has been hindered by limited spectral range and poor single-photon indistinguishability. Here, we demonstrate a reproducible approach for generating near-infrared (1090–1200 nm) quantum emitters in bilayer MoTe2 using deterministic strain and defect engineering. These emitters exhibit strong linear polarization, sub-nanosecond lifetimes, high single-photon purity (triggered g(2)(0) as low as ~0.01 under p-shell excitation), and resolution-limited emission. Electrostatic biasing enables spectral tuning, suppresses photon bunching, and shortens radiative lifetimes. Most notably, two-photon interference measurements reveal a Hong-Ou-Mandel visibility of ~7.1%, and up to ~60% with post-selection under p-shell excitation, which represents state-of-the-art performance for quantum emitters in the transition-metal dichalcogenide platform. These results establish MoTe2 as a viable platform for tunable, low-noise, high-purity single-photon sources for quantum photonics.

title: From biological principles to battery interfaces: recent progress in bio-inspired design for aqueous zinc-ion batteries

Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

Regional infrastructure repurposing: Pathways from assessment to geothermal energy production and storage
abstract: Addressing the growing demand for sustainable energy, we explore the innovative potential of repurposing existing subsurface infrastructure for geothermal energy production and energy storage. We present an integrated technical, economic, and legal framework for repurposing regional-scale infrastructure to systematically evaluate and optimize geothermal resource utilization. The states of Berlin and Brandenburg in Germany serve as a model area, with field studies in Groß Schönebeck and Lusatia demonstrating practical infrastructure repurposing. Results show that 12 of the 17 evaluated wells are potentially suitable for repurposing, with hydrothermal energy (HE) emerging as the most promising option. Economic viability is achievable by targeting the Middle Buntsandstein formation at depths exceeding 2400 meters and temperatures above 86 ∘ C, utilizing well doublets with a minimum of 750-meter spacing. Reservoir simulations indicate that optimized development schemes can achieve gross thermal power ranging from 2.9 to 7.6 M W t h with a Levelized Cost of Heat (LCOH) ranging from € 0.035/kWh to € 0.08/kWh. This is achievable through exploration near existing wells and direct connection to district heating networks. While Borehole Heat Exchangers (BHEs) offer faster implementation, their economic viability is challenging due to low thermal power and proximity requirements. Recognizing a mismatch between existing subsurface data and heat demand areas, the Landesamt für Bergbau, Geologie und Rohstoffe (LBGR) has initiated a new 2D seismic exploration campaign in 2025 for the Lower Lusatia area, leveraging well-established district heating and hydrocarbon infrastructure. This research demonstrates an economic strategy for reusing infrastructure for heating and energy storage, supported by strategic government initiatives, and provides a replicable decision-making workflow to guide geothermal energy development.

Solvent Cage Suppresses Dynamically Induced Entropic Pathways to Provide High Selectivity in Intramolecular Fe-Oxo Radical Rebound Reactions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract For homogeneous transition metal reactions, it is generally assumed that when intermediates are formed, they are sufficiently long-lived for the surrounding solvent cage to fully equilibrate prior to product formation. However, some transition metal reactions generate a highly reactive and transient intermediate for which product selectivity is not governed by subsequent competing transition states but rather by dynamic effects during descent from the transition state that forms the intermediate. In such reactions, solvent reorganization may be slow relative to product formation, which could significantly impact reaction pathway selectivity. Here, we demonstrate the important role of the solvent cage and explicit solute–solvent interactions in determining pathway selectivity for the ultrafast-evolving radical pair intermediate generated during (PDP)Fe-oxo-catalyzed intramolecular sp3 C–H functionalization. Quasiclassical reactive trajectories showed that with only a continuum solvent model a mixture of oxygen rebound/hydroxylation, desaturation, and direct carboxylate rebound products are formed due to dynamically driven, entropically favored wandering, which is inconsistent with experiments. In contrast, trajectories in explicit solvent reproduced the experimental product selectivity and demonstrated that solvent controls the nonstatistical, motion-driven selectivity by acting as a nonequilibrated solvent cage that restricts access to entropically favorable wandering configurations. The solvent effectively guides the radical pair intermediate toward one dominant product pathway. These results demonstrate the important role of the solvent cage in reactions involving highly transient intermediates where dynamic effects control selectivity.

title: Lithium–Oxygen Batteries: Fundamental and Practical Considerations
abstract: Abstract Lithium–oxygen batteries (LOBs) have emerged as a compelling next-generation energy storage technology for aviation due to their high theoretical energy densities and the use of abundant oxygen as a cathode reactant. Unlike conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), which are limited by the mass of intercalation materials and one-electron redox processes, LOBs leverage multielectron oxygen redox chemistry to achieve gravimetric energy density exceeding 3,500 Wh kgLi2O2–1 based on lithium peroxide and up to 5,200 Wh kgLi2O–1 for lithium oxide. However, practical implementation of LOBs remains constrained by significant challenges including low round-trip efficiency and low system-level energy density, the latter arising from the need for oxygen management in both open and closed architectures. The electrolyte viscosity, oxygen solubility, volatility, and chemical stability toward reactive oxygen species can profoundly influence discharge capacity, rate capability, reversibility, and long-term stability. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of recent progress in LOBs, focusing on electrolyte designs, electrode engineering, and strategies for mitigating parasitic reactions as well as the interplay between material-level properties and system-level constraints, offering a critical perspective on the path toward realizing high-energy, practical LOB systems.

title: Atomically Dispersed In 3+ Anchored on Rigid MOF‐808 for Highly Selective CO 2 Electroreduction with Long‐Term Stability in Acidic Media
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) reduction offers a promising pathway for carbon utilization but is severely hindered by the aggressive hydrogen evolution reaction and the structural instability of main‐group metal catalysts in strong acidic solution. Herein, we report the precise anchoring of atomically dispersed In 3+ onto the inorganic nodes of MOF‐808, achieving an extraordinarily high loading of 21.8 wt%. The rigid framework of MOF‐808 has abundant open metal sites that securely coordinate with In 3+ , while its well‐defined 1.8 nm pores ensure rapid mass transport during electrocatalysis. Mechanistic studies reveal that intense electronic coupling of In 3+ with the Zr 6 ‐oxo clusters efficiently improves the local electronic structure of the isolated In 3+ sites. Consequently, the high In 3+ density delivers exceptional performance for selective CO 2 reduction to formic acid in acidic electrolyte, achieving an outstanding Faradaic efficiency of 97.1% at −1.2 V vs. RHE. More importantly, the robust spatial confinement for the anchored In 3+ within the framework efficiently prevents their chemical leaching and reductive migration, enabling an outstanding long‐term stability of 216 h. This study demonstrates an effective strategy for constructing highly stable and atomically dispersed In 3+ catalysts for electrochemical applications in acidic media.

title: Photocatalyst Design for Plastic Upcycling: From Polymer Deconstruction to Selective Valorization
abstract: ABSTRACT Plastic waste poses a severe threat to our environment, yet represents an abundant and largely underutilized reservoir of chemically processed carbon and embedded energy. Photocatalytic conversion offers a promising route to valorize plastic waste into fuels and value‐added chemicals. However, practical plastic photovalorization remains severely limited by sluggish polymer deconstruction and poor product selectivity. These challenges are further complicated by diverse polymer structures and crystallinity, which dictate distinct conversion strategies and impose varied requirements on photocatalysts. In this review, we map photocatalytic plastic upcycling across major plastic categories to establish the relationships between polymer properties, conversion routes, and the corresponding photocatalyst requirements. On this basis, we focus on photocatalyst design from polymer deconstruction to selective product formation, highlighting material design strategies for improving polymer accessibility and deconstruction, regulating selective intermediate conversion, and coordinating coupled redox reactions. We further detail the selective formation of value‐added oxygenates, hydrocarbons, aromatics, and C─N products, with particular emphasis on how active‐site engineering of photocatalysts directs the corresponding reaction pathways. Finally, key material and system challenges in plastic photovalorization, including real‐world plastic feedstock complexity, low carbon efficiency, process viability, and scale‐up, are highlighted. Future perspectives are discussed to guide the development of practical plastic photovalorization systems.

abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Disruptions to leading-strand synthesis impair and stall replication forks because DNA synthesis by the leading-strand polymerase, Pol ε, is essential for optimal template unwinding by the replicative CMG (CDC45–MCM–GINS) helicase
                    1,2
                    . Failure to efficiently restart and/or protect stalled replication forks is a major source of genomic instability
                    3–6
                    . Stalled forks can be restarted by a variety of mechanisms, including repriming downstream of the impediment
                    4
                    . In human cells, the primase–polymerase PRIMPOL promotes fork progression during replication stress
                    7–10
                    , but how its activity is coordinated by the replisome is unresolved. Here, by reconstituting replication fork stalling and restart with purified human proteins, we show that the CMG helicase directs PRIMPOL for efficient replication fork restart. Unexpectedly, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A
                    9,11
                    is not critical for fork restart in this system. We show that PRIMPOL binds directly to CMG, and a cryo-electron microscopy structure illustrates how this targets PRIMPOL specifically for leading-strand priming to minimize the size of post-replicative gaps. Ablating the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction abolishes fork restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent DNA damage tolerance in human cells. Our work establishes PRIMPOL as an integrated component of the human replisome dedicated to leading-strand priming.

title: Plasmonically Enhanced Microarray Immunoassay for High‐Sensitivity Monitoring of Heart Failure
abstract: ABSTRACT Point‑of‑care testing (POCT) demands diagnostic platforms that pair high analytical sensitivity with compact, low‑cost readout hardware, yet fluorescence‑based immunoassays face a fundamental tradeoff between detector cost and detection performance. Plasmonic nanocavities—such as metal–dielectric–metal nanopatch antennas—offer a powerful signal‑amplification strategy by dramatically enhancing fluorophore emission, enabling sensitive fluorescence detection with inexpensive optics. Here, we introduce a plasmonically enhanced fluorescence microarray immunoassay that integrates nanopatch antennas for high‑sensitivity, low‑cost quantification of key heart‑failure biomarkers, NT‑proBNP, NGAL, and galectin‑3, using a custom smartphone‑based detector. The nanopatch antennas yield up to 485‑fold fluorescence enhancement enabling quantitative and multiplexed detection with limits of detection of 0.055, 3.932, and 0.864 ng/mL, respectively. Analysis of NT‑proBNP–positive human samples shows strong correlation with clinically validated assays, demonstrating the potential of this plasmonically enhanced platform to deliver high‑performance heart‑failure biomarker monitoring at low cost in resource‑limited and point‑of‑care settings.
