title: Anti -Dihydroxylation-Enabled Dual-Resolution Profiling and Imaging of Fatty Acid C═C Bond Isomers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Lipids are essential for membrane structure, signaling, and stress adaptation. Their diverse biological roles are largely dictated by the presence of C═C bonds in unsaturated fatty acids (FAs), which vary in both position and geometry. However, unambiguous characterization and in situ mapping of these two structural features have remained longstanding analytical challenges. Here, we present a stereochemistry-preserved chemical derivatization strategy coupled with trapped ion mobility spectrometry-tandem MS (TIMS-MS/MS), enabling complete resolution of both FA C═C bond position and geometry within a single workflow. This approach facilitates rapid and quantitative profiling of dynamic cis–trans isomerization in bacteria under diverse stress conditions and, notably, reveals a previously unrecognized dose-dependent antibiotic adaptation mechanism in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a multidrug-resistant pathogen. To translate this strategy to spatially resolved analyses, we developed an in situ derivatization workflow for mass spectrometry imaging, which uncovers the spatial heterogeneity of FA isomers in proximally cocultured, clinically relevant polymicrobial pathogens. These findings highlight colony-specific spatial dynamics of cis and trans lipid isomers and suggest lipid-mediated metabolic interactions between co-occurring microbial species. Together, this integrated platform enables both quantitative and spatial interrogation of lipid isomerization, providing new opportunities to systematically investigate its roles in microbial physiology, pathogenesis, and beyond.

title: Conjugate Chiral Carbon Dots for Scalable Asymmetric Photocatalysis in Flow
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as scalable, metal-free photocatalysts, but their use as conjugate organo-photocatalysts for enantioselective chemistry remains unexplored. Here, we covalently anchor a chiral imidazolidinone organocatalyst to amorphous, citric acid-derived CDs, giving a colloidal conjugate that acts as both photosensitizer and enantiodetermining component. This chiral CD material promotes the asymmetric radical α-alkylation of aldehydes in up to 84% yield and 93% e.e. Its semihomogeneous nature enables catalyst recovery by precipitation and reuse over five cycles with only minor loss in yield and e.e. The well-dispersed conjugate is also compatible with continuous photoflow, where Bayesian optimization in only 10 experiments enabled a gram-scale reaction in 80% yield and 91% e.e. This work establishes chiral conjugate CDs as a practical, recoverable platform for sustainable asymmetric photocatalysis.

title: Reprogramming ThDP-Dependent Enzyme for Intermolecular [3 + 2] Annulation via a Homoenolate Intermediate
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Thiamine diphosphate (ThDP)-dependent enzymes are versatile biocatalysts for carbon–carbon bond formation, yet their catalytic repertoire has been largely confined to linear homologation and intramolecular cyclizations that rely on single-site reactive intermediates such as the Breslow or ketyl radical species. Intermolecular annulation─a powerful strategy for constructing cyclic architectures─has remained elusive within this enzyme class. Here, we report the first intermolecular [3 + 2] annulation catalyzed by a ThDP-dependent enzyme, achieved through a homoenolate-mediated nucleophilic addition pathway. A phylogeny-guided enzyme mining identified a previously uncharacterized enzyme from Variovorax boronicumulans(ThDP-5), and subsequent protein engineering yielded the F484S variant, which exhibits markedly enhanced activity and exquisite stereocontrol. This biocatalytic system exhibits a broad substrate scope (30 examples), accommodating diverse substituted cinnamaldehydes and isatins to afford chiral spirooxindole lactones with excellent stereoselectivity (up to > 20:1 dr and 99% ee). Preparative-scale reactions (2 mmol) validate its synthetic utility. This work expands ThDP-dependent biocatalysis to intermolecular annulations, providing a robust and selective platform for the construction of pharmaceutically relevant spirocyclic architectures.

title: Interfacial Confinement Enables Conformal IrOx Nanofilms for Low-Ir-Loading PEM Water Electrolysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Terawatt-scale deployment of proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) requires low iridium (Ir) loading, which disrupts the catalyst layer’s in-plane electronic percolation network and severely degrades performance. Here, we overcome this bottleneck via an interfacial confinement strategy that electrostatically enriches cationic Ir intermediates on the negatively charged, oxygen-deficient TiOx surface, thereby redirecting Ir deposition from three-dimensional island growth to a two-dimensional conformal film on TiO2 supports. The resulting IrOx-NF@TiO2 catalyst with low Ir packing density maintains long-range in-plane electron percolation, reducing reliance on the high Ir loading typically required by conventional IrOx nanoparticle catalysts to establish quasi-continuous conductive pathways. At a loading of 0.166 mgIr cm−2, blade-coated membrane electrode assemblies incorporating this architecture feature ∼7 μm-thick catalyst layers with an Ir packing density of only ∼0.25 gIr cm–3, allowing an ∼84% reduction in Ir use while achieving performance comparable to that of commercial IrO2. This work highlights the potential of supported conformal IrOx catalysts as competitive candidates for next-generation low-Ir PEMWEs.

title: Solvent/Anion Codepleted Solvation Engineering Enables Low-Coordination Electrolytes for High-Energy and Low-Temperature Sodium-Ion Pouch Cells
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Widespread deployment of sodium-ion batteries demands both high energy density and reliable low-temperature (LT) operation, but is constrained by a persistent trade-off between high-voltage stability (cathode/electrolyte) and LT ion-transport kinetics. Herein, we report a solvent/anion codepleted solvation engineering strategy to construct low-coordination electrolytes through competitive anion complexation mediated by a bulky electron-deficient additive, TMSB (tris(trimethylsilyl)borate). We reveal that TMSB preferentially complexes with PF6– to suppress direct anion-Na+ coordination, while its bulky steric backbone disrupts conventional ion-pair networks and restricts excessive solvent-Na+ coordination. This strategy fundamentally boosts ionic conductivity (from 2.41 to 5.34 mS cm–1) and lowers the desolvation energy barrier (from 44.82 to 33.97 kJ mol–1). Moreover, such a strategy enables a high-modulus (2.7 GPa), inorganic-rich cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI), which can not only mitigate surface degradation, but also suppress bulk phase transitions of cathode materials. Consequently, the electrolyte demonstrates broad compatibility across diverse cathodes (NFM, NVP, and P2-NNMO) under extreme voltage (up to 4.5 V) and temperature (−40 to 25 °C) conditions. Remarkably, the scaled-up 6.8 Ah pouch cell achieves a record-high energy density of 200 Wh kg–1 at 25 °C, while maintaining 162 Wh kg–1 even at −20 °C, offering a generalizable molecular paradigm for extreme-environment energy storage.

title: A Single Water Molecule Drives a 20-Fold Acceleration in the Gas-Phase Reaction of Iodide with Ozone
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Iodine chemistry has an outsized role in the atmosphere and environment due to its highly reactive nature. Unlike chlorine and bromine, around 80% of atmospheric iodine is emitted directly from the ocean through the reaction of iodide and ozone at the sea surface. Uncertainties remain, however, in the effects of hydration, salinity, temperature, and other factors on this globally significant reaction. Using linear ion-trap mass spectrometry, a single water molecule is shown here to provide a 23 (±6)-fold acceleration to the rate of iodide oxidation. The first step in reaction of both I– and I–·H2O with ozone is oxidation to IO– with subsequent fast reactions to yield IO3–. No evidence is found for direct routes from I–·H2O to IO2– nor any incorporation of the water oxygen into ionic products. Ab initio calculations show that the initial rate-determining step for both reactions proceeds on the singlet surface with water playing an active role to lower the barrier through hydrogen bonding. Kinetic modeling based on the computed energetics is in excellent agreement with experimental measurements and enables extrapolation of this reaction to lower temperatures relevant to polar regions and the ozone layer. This analysis shows that (i) I– may outcompete I• for ozone destruction as temperature decreases, and (ii) I–·H2O reacts more than an order of magnitude faster than I• over 350 to 230 K. This work demonstrates that iodide has a previously underappreciated role in multiphase ozone destruction in the atmosphere and lays the foundation for understanding microscopic environmental influences in salt clusters and nanodroplets.

title: A Multimetallic Single-Atom Catalyst on a Defective Graphene Support toward Methanol Oxidation and Oxygen Reduction Reactions: Density Functional Theory, Machine Learning, and Experiments
abstract: Abstract Multimetallic single-atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as promising candidates for electrocatalytic reactions. However, identifying bifunctional multimetallic SACs capable of efficiently catalyzing both the oxygen reduction and methanol oxidation reactions (ORR and MOR), applicable to direct methanol fuel cells, remains challenging due to the vast compositional design space. Here, we propose a defective graphene-supported multimetallic SAC (M1M2M3M4M5-SAC) incorporating Mn, Pt, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cu for simultaneous MOR and ORR catalysis. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations along with machine learning (ML) predictions reveal that the Co active site in PtFeNiCoCu-SAC delivers the most favorable performance, exhibiting ORR and MOR overpotentials of 0.47 and 0.46 V, respectively. Guided by these insights, we synthesized PtFeNiCoCu-SAC and a nitrogen-doped sample, confirming their atomic structures using X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Electrochemical measurements validate the theoretical predictions: PtFeNiCoCu-SAC achieves an experimental ORR overpotential of 0.30 VRHE and a Tafel slope of 114 mV/dec at –1 mA/cm2, along with a half-wave potential of 0.86 VRHE. This catalyst also demonstrates good MOR activity, with a pronounced oxidation peak at 0.97 VRHE. Therefore, this work establishes a DFT- and ML-guided strategy for the accelerated rational design of multimetallic SACs and highlights PtFeNiCoCu-SAC as a promising bifunctional catalyst for energy-conversion applications.

title: n -Value-Tuned Quasi-2D Perovskites for Wavelength-Selective Optoelectronic Synapses
abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic vision systems demand optoelectronic synapses that combine wavelength-selective sensing with gradual and linear synaptic weight updates. In two-dimensional (2D) halide perovskites, extending visible-light absorption can be accompanied by accelerating ion migration and premature current saturation. Here, we regulate the phase composition of quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) BA2MA(n–1)PbnI(3n+1) perovskites by tuning the nominal n value. Incorporation of the n = 2 phase extends the absorption edge from 525 nm (green) to approximately 600 nm (red), enabling distinguishable responses under blue, green, and red illumination. The nominal n = 1.2 composition provides sufficient higher-n phase for red-light absorption while suppressing excessive ion migration, yielding highly linear photocurrent weight updates. Using these wavelength-, intensity-, and duration-dependent responses, we construct a light-history regression model that maps accumulated exposure to electrical blue-light-hazard warning and literature-derived phototoxicity thresholds under different color temperatures. This phase-engineering strategy provides a material-level route to integrate spectral selectivity and linear signal integration in neuromorphic vision systems.

title: Integrated 3D Porous Copper@BiSb Alloy Anodes via Pulse Electrodeposition for High-Performance Potassium-Ion Storage
abstract: Abstract Antimony (Sb) and bismuth (Bi) are promising alloy-type anode materials for potassium-ion batteries (PIBs), yet Sb suffers from a massive 390% volume expansion during potassiation, while Bi is limited by a relatively low specific capacity of 384 mAh·g–1. Moreover, existing synthesis methods for BiSb alloys are complex, costly, and require binders or conductive additives that impair electrochemical performance. Herein, we innovatively fabricate an integrated 3D porous copper@BiSb (3DPC@BiSb) electrode by pulse electrodepositing BiSb alloy onto a 3D porous copper (3DPC) substrate. The 3DPC scaffold provides abundant active sites, shortens ion diffusion pathways, and mitigates volume expansion, while the binder-free design eliminates interfacial issues. Electrochemical tests demonstrate that the 3DPC@BiSb electrode delivers a reversible capacity of 400.6 mAh·g–1 at 0.1 A·g–1 after 100 cycles and retains 205.0 mAh·g–1 even at 32 C, outperforming most reported alloy-type anodes for PIBs. Kinetic analysis, ex-situ X-ray diffraction, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the superior performance originates from the synergistic effect of Sb (high capacity) and Bi (structural stability), enhanced K+ adsorption energy, and reduced diffusion barrier. This work provides a scalable strategy for fabricating integrated alloy anodes capable of large-area electrode preparation. It offers insights into the structure-performance relationship of BiSb-based materials, advancing the development of high-performance thin-film PIBs for renewable energy storage.

title: A Repeatable Supramolecular Adhesive with Ultrastrong Underwater Adhesion, Self-Healing Ability, and Long-Term Stability
abstract: Abstract Repeatable adhesives attract enormous attention for their environmental friendliness and adaptability but suffer from weak adhesion when used in underwater conditions. Herein, we develop a supramolecular adhesive by incorporating quadruple hydrogen-bonded units into isocyanate-modified polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) polymers. By synergistically utilizing interfacial covalent bonds and multiple hydrogen bonds, the supramolecular adhesive exhibits repeatable adhesion in air for at least 5 cycles and ultrastrong underwater adhesion of ∼9.37 MPa. The rapid establishment of covalent bonds on various substrate surfaces confers the adhesive with instantaneous and tough adhesion in both air and underwater environments. Reversible multiple hydrogen bonds within the adhesive polymers endow the material with self-healing performance. In addition, rheology analysis combined with mechanical tests revealed the thermal-responsive property of the adhesive. Taking advantage of the self-healing performance and thermal-responsive adhesion, the adhesive exhibits repeatable ability. This work deepens the understanding of multiple hydrogen bonds and isocyanate-modified PDMS polymers, enabling the fabrication of repeatable adhesives for industrial applications.

title: Strain Gradient Engineering at Material Interfaces: Flexocatalysis Beyond Centrosymmetry
abstract: Abstract The flexoelectric effect, an electromechanical coupling phenomenon ubiquitous in all materials (including centrosymmetric crystals) under non-uniform strain gradients, has recently given rise to the emerging field of flexocatalysis. By eliminating the need for external light or electrical biases and circumventing the symmetry constraints of piezoelectric materials, it represents a catalytic paradigm for green chemistry, with applications spanning water splitting for hydrogen production, hydrogen peroxide generation, pollutant degradation, and biomedical therapies (e.g., tumor treatment). This review systematically outlines the fundamentals of the flexoelectric effect and the strain gradient-driven charge separation mechanisms. Recent advances in representative applications across energy, environmental, and biomedical fields are comprehensively summarized. Additionally, preliminary strategies to enhance catalytic efficiency are categorized into two main approaches: (1) amplifying the flexoelectric response, primarily interface engineering, the synergistic coupling of piezoelectric and flexoelectric effects, and doping; and (2) optimizing charge separation and transfer, mainly via introduction of vacancies, photo-flexoelectric synergistic coupling, and single-atom modification. Finally, the current challenges and future opportunities of flexocatalysis are highlighted, providing a foundational roadmap that bridges solid-state physics and interfacial catalysis.

title: Room-Temperature Phosphorescent Materials Based on β-Diketone Derivatives Exhibiting Excitation- & Concentration-Dependent Characteristics
abstract: Abstract Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have attracted extensive attention owing to their potential applications in chemical sensing, optoelectronic devices, bioimaging, and information encryption. However, developing RTP materials with dynamically tunable emission colors that respond to multiple external stimuli remains a significant challenge. In this work, BA@TTA composites were constructed by doping 2-thenoyltrifluoroacetone (TTA) guest molecules into a boric acid (BA) host matrix, exhibiting efficient room-temperature afterglow. Upon changing the excitation wavelength from 254 nm to 365 nm, the afterglow emission color can be tuned from blue to yellow, indicating prominent excitation-wavelength-dependent luminescence behavior. Moreover, with increasing TTA content, the yellow afterglow under 365 nm excitation is gradually enhanced, whereas the blue afterglow component under 254 nm excitation remains nearly unchanged. This excitation- & concentration-dependent color-tunable phosphorescence of BA@TTA originates from the coexistence of isolated and aggregated TTA species, in which efficient intermolecular energy transfer and aggregation-induced electronic interactions reduce the excited-state energy gap, enhance spin–orbit coupling, and accelerate intersystem crossing, thereby enabling color-tunable room-temperature phosphorescence. This universal mechanism is extended to other β-diketone derivatives for high-security multi-level information encryption.

title: Photoelectrochemical CO2 Reduction to CO by a Molecular Catalyst Attached to Pyrene-Terminated Silicon through Noncovalent Interactions
abstract: Abstract A ruthenium-based CO2 reduction catalyst immobilized on a Si photocathode through noncovalent π–π interactions is active for the photochemical conversion of CO2 to CO, with 34% ± 20% Faradaic efficiency with current densities of j = –(0.3 ± 0.1) mA cm–2 at –1.9 V vs Fc+/0 in an acetonitrile/water electrolyte solution under 1 sun illumination. Si photocathodes were functionalized with pyrene (p-Si–Py) using a Grignard methodology. A previously reported CO2 reduction catalyst, [Ru(tpy)(Mebim-py)(NCCH3)][PF6]2 (tpy = 2,2′:6′,2″-terpyridine, Mebim-py = 1-methylbenzimidazol-2-ylidene-3-(2′-pyridine)) was modified to include a pyrene moiety in the terpyridine backbone, enabling π–π stacking of the catalyst onto the Si surface to achieve a surface coverage of (1.85 ± 0.28) x 10–12 mol cm–2 (ca. 2% to 5% of a monolayer) as quantified via inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy (ICP-MS). A 420 mV photovoltage (Vph) was quantified for the p-Si–Py photocathode. Measurements of charge carrier recombination kinetics through time-resolved infrared spectroscopy indicate that surface attachment of pyrene moieties introduces defects at the Si interface, even without the presence of the catalyst. These defects provide competing kinetic pathways for photogenerated carriers, hypothesized to influence the selectivity of the hybrid photoelectrode, an important implication for future designs of hybrid photoelectrodes.

title: Berberine/Verteporfin Nanomicelles Enable O2-Economized Photodynamic Immunotherapy in Esophageal Cancer Via Tumor Metabolic Remodeling
abstract: Abstract Photodynamic therapy (PDT) can convert oxidative damage into systemic antitumor immunity, but mitochondrial oxygen consumption, lactate accumulation, and aberrant angiogenesis create a hypoxic and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that limits treatment. Here, berberine (BBR) and verteporfin (VER) were co-loaded into nanomicelles (BV NMs) through sonication-assisted self-assembly of PEG-g-(PVAc-co-PVCL), creating a “microenvironment remodeling—PDT potentiation—immune activation” strategy. BV NMs had a hydrodynamic diameter of 56.15 ± 0.30 nm. Drug loading lowered the critical micelle concentration from 11.2 μg/mL (blank micelles) to an apparent 1.3 μg/mL (BV NMs), supporting dilution stability. It also enhanced aqueous dispersibility, cellular uptake, and intratumoral accumulation. Mechanistically, BBR reduced mitochondrial complex I-associated activity, intracellular adenosine triphosphate levels, and extracellular lactate accumulation, attenuated cellular hypoxia and hypoxia-inducible factor-1α responses, and increased intracellular oxygen availability. Before irradiation, VER suppressed Yes-associated protein signaling and vascular endothelial growth factor expression, providing light-independent antitumor and antiangiogenic regulation. Under 660 nm irradiation, VER induced reactive oxygen species accumulation, mitochondrial depolarization, tumor-cell death, and immunogenic cell death. In vivo, BV NMs combined with irradiation achieved an approximately 96% inhibition rate based on terminal tumor weight. Proportions of mature dendritic cells in tumor-draining lymph nodes and splenic CD8+ T cells reached 3.33 and 2.73 times the control levels, respectively, alongside expansion of memory CD8+ T-cell populations. Treatment also reduced experimental pulmonary metastatic burden, achieved 50% survival at day 60, and caused no evident short-term systemic toxicity. This platform couples metabolic and angiogenic regulation with oxygen-dependent PDT and antitumor immunity, providing a strategy against primary and metastatic tumors.

title: Reticular Materials as Optical Sensors of Volatile Organic Compounds for Healthcare and Environmental Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are a family of molecules that possess high vapor pressure and are regarded as air pollutants that prevail in both indoor and outdoor settings. Prolonged exposure to VOCs poses a serious risk to human health. On the other hand, VOCs emitted by humans and plants have been recognized as key biomarkers to estimate the status of health and physiology in living beings. Profiling the total content of VOCs in human and plant fluids leads to early diagnosis of diseases and timely treatment. Monitoring the presence of VOCs, either to track air pollution or to estimate the status of health, has therefore commanded increasing attention. Among the various techniques, optical sensing methods have been sought after owing to the considerations of their fast response time, versatility, miniaturization and portability, as well as the possibility of performing non-invasive detection. Advanced functional materials, such as porous reticular solids, including metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), and hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs), are well suited not only as sorbents for the detection and capture of VOCs but also as suitable substrates for various approaches of optical signaling. This review, through recent case studies, presents the advances in the optical sensing of VOCs by reticular materials. In addition, a comparative analysis between various reticular material types has been provided, along with an outline of the current challenges and the opportunities that exist for future research.

title: Harmonized Na-Site Occupancy and Fe Local Structure in a Mixed-Phosphate Cathode for All-Climate Sodium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 (NFPP) has attracted considerable attention as a low-cost, structurally stable cathode for sodium-ion batteries. However, its commercialization is severely hampered by electrochemically inert impurities from conventional synthesis and insufficient energy density. Herein, we report a heteroatom-free strategy combining precursor pathway engineering with Na-site regulation and local Fe-environment modulation to synthesize a phase-pure NFPP-type cathode using a nominal Na3.67Fe2.67(PO4)1.67(P2O7) precursor stoichiometry. The resulting N3.67F2.67PP sample exhibits distinct Na-site occupancies from conventional NFPP. Theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations demonstrate that increased occupation ratios of Na4 and Na2 sites collectively elevate the discharge voltage plateau and enhance cycling stability. Meanwhile, precise regulation of the Na/Fe/PO4/P2O7 ratio modulates the electronic structure of Fe and increases Fe–O coordination disorder, markedly boosting Na+ migration kinetics and electronic conductivity. Consequently, the optimized material delivers a high specific capacity of 110.4 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C, retains 98.6% of its capacity after 1700 cycles at 1 C, and exhibits an impressive 103.5 mAh g–1 at 10 C. It also exhibits superior performance over a wide temperature range from –40 to 60 °C. Notably, Ah-level pouch and cylindrical batteries assembled with kilogram-scale materials achieve outstanding performance, highlighting a practical route toward commercialization. This work clarifies the structure–property relationship of NFPP-based materials and provides valuable guidance for designing high-performance mixed-phosphate cathodes.

title: Repurposing Grain Boundaries for Graphene Origami Auxetic Metamaterials with Enhanced Fatigue Resistance
abstract: Abstract Graphene represents the pinnacle of intrinsic material strength, yet it remains functionally limited by a lack of plasticity and severe degradation in mechanical performance associated with porosity-driven upscaling. Although graphene origami (GOri) offers a deterministic alternative to porous networks, its realization has been restricted to chemically functionalized, metastable frameworks. Here, we demonstrate a computational design strategy that repurposes grain boundaries (GBs) observed in large-scale chemical vapor deposited (CVD) graphene as topological precursors for stable GOri structures. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we show that periodic pentagon–heptagon (5–7) ring arrays within the tilted GBs can facilitate out-of-plane corrugations of the graphene domains, mimicking macroscopic folding creases without chemical modification. Our study also shows that the mechanical response of the proposed structure is highly tunable via linear grain size (µ) and dimensionless aspect ratio (α), enabling a wide range of control over tensile strength, elastic modulus, and negative Poisson’s ratio (NPR), reaching –3.77. Furthermore, the developed GB-GOri architecture achieves a 20% enhancement in fatigue strength and a fatigue life exceeding 150% of that of functionalized counterparts through pseudo-plastic deformation. Effectively, this GB-assisted defect engineering promotes stable crack growth and provides proof-of-concept for the future experimental fabrication of graphene-based auxetic metamaterials.

title: Microfluidic Control of Biomolecular Condensate Growth Reveals Scaling Crossover and Interfacial Regulation
abstract: Abstract Biomolecular condensates, formed via phase separation, play vital roles in cellular organization, yet their nucleation and growth dynamics remain poorly understood, particularly under controlled physiological conditions. Here, we employ a microfluidic platform to precisely manipulate the nucleation and growth of PGL-3 protein condensates at fluid–solid interfaces. We demonstrate that ionic strength and co-phase-separating proteins (SEPA-1) robustly tune the nucleation rate without altering the long-term growth scaling ∼tn. Single-condensate tracking further resolves a dynamic scaling crossover from rapid isolated growth with n ≃ 1/2 to diffusion-limited collective growth with n ≃ 1/3, consistent with simulations of overlapping protein-depletion fields. Furthermore, we show that this classical scaling breaks down during viscoelastic phase separation, where elastic-dominated condensates exhibit a significantly reduced exponent. Our work establishes molecular modulation and interfacial mechanics as key regulators of condensate dynamics, revealing physical principles that govern the size and material state of biological condensates.

title: Engineering Ambipolar Charge Transport in Stable Solution-Processed Nanofilms of Electrically Conductive Liquid-Crystalline Anthraquinones
abstract: Abstract The realization of ambipolar charge transport with long-term operational and environmental stability of the transport layer is a rarely addressed challenge in organic electronics, especially with respect to solution-processed devices. This study reports the molecular engineering of redox-active liquid-crystalline anthraquinones with triazole and cyanovinylene functional units to stabilize ordered columnar mesophases at room temperature. In addition to high thermal stability, solution-processed nanofilms of these discotic liquid crystals (DLCs) also demonstrate effective charge-extraction from injecting electrodes in diode devices, with their electrical conductivity values among the highest reported for DLC nanofilms (10–4 S/m). Alongside ultra-stable electrical performance over repeated electrical cycling, these devices exhibit long-term stability for up to two years without encapsulation under ambient storage conditions. Balanced ambipolarity is achieved via the fabrication of single-carrier devices where hole and electron mobilities both match at an order of 10–3 cm2/Vs. Being a pioneering report dedicated to detailed electrical conductivity studies and ambient stability of solution-processed ambipolar DLC films, the present work enriches the scope of practical DLC-based electronic devices from the fundamental viewpoint of molecular design.

title: Fe-Regulated Sulfidation of Ni-MOF to Construct an Fe-Ni(OH)2/Ni3S2 Heterojunction for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution in Both Acidic and Alkaline Media
abstract: Abstract Developing efficient and durable non-precious electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in both acidic and alkaline media is a critical challenge. Herein, we report a Fe-regulated sulfidation strategy that converts a Ni-MOF precursor into a Fe-doped Ni(OH)2/Ni3S2 heterojunction catalyst. Fe acts as a kinetic phase regulator that suppresses the complete conversion of Ni(OH)2 into Ni3S2, stabilizing a mixed phase architecture with abundant heterointerfaces and enlarged electrochemically active surface area. The optimized catalyst delivers exceptional HER performance, requiring overpotentials of only 163.3 mV at –10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and 214.3 mV at –100 mA cm−2 in 0.5 M H2SO4, along with outstanding durability (200 h at –500 mA cm−2 in alkaline electrolyte and 100 h at –100 mA cm−2 in acidic electrolyte). Post-stability characterizations reveal pH-dependent reconstruction: under alkaline conditions, the Ni(OH)2 phase partially dissolves while the Ni3S2 framework remains; under acidic conditions, Fe2+ oxidation to Fe3+ forms a protective M-OH-rich oxide layer on Ni3S2. Density functional theory calculations identify Ni as the primary active site, with Fe functioning as an electronic modulator that redistributes electron density toward Ni and optimizes the d-band center. In alkaline media, the cooperative charge effect and upshifted d-band center synergistically promote water dissociation, with OH* desorption identified as the rate-determining step; in acidic media, strong electrostatic attraction from the highly negatively charged Ni sites dominates H* adsorption. This work highlights the pivotal role of heterojunction engineering and phase regulation in designing durable pH-universal HER catalysts.

title: Electric-Field-Driven Surface Ionic Transport on Hydroxylated SiO2 Governs Transient Leakage and Hybrid Bonding Reliability
abstract: Abstract Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding is critical for 3D integrated circuit packaging, where dielectric surface activation impacts bonding quality and long-term reliability. NaOH-based wet chemical activation is a promising approach for a scalable and cost-effective processing under ambient conditions. However, this route introduces residual ions at the SiO2 surface, raising concerns regarding electrical leakage and dielectric stability. In this study, electric-field-driven surface ionic transport on NaOH-activated SiO2 and its role in transient leakage and hybrid bonding reliability were investigated. Reversible and polarity-dependent transient current peaks observed in cyclic electrical measurements provide evidence for electric-field-driven migration of the mobile ionic species at the SiO2 interface. In addition, higher NaOH concentrations promoted greater residual Na+ accumulation and intensified transient leakage peaks, supporting the selection of 0.5 M NaOH as an effective activation condition. Systematic decoupling experiments demonstrate that residual mobile Na+ ions are the dominant contributors to the transient leakage current rather than fixed hydroxyl groups. Quantitative analysis reveals Na+ surface mobility of approximately 3 × 10–10 m2V–1s–1, an order-of-magnitude upper-bound estimate that is consistent between constant-bias and ramped-bias measurements and about six orders of magnitude higher than that in bulk SiO2, suggesting a surface-dominated transport. An optimized 3 min deionized water (DI) rinse reduces the mobile Na+ population below the electrical detection limit and decreases the Na 1s XPS intensity by roughly an order of magnitude, suppressing the transient leakage to near-baseline levels while maintaining hydrophilicity and achieving the SiO2–SiO2 bonding strength of 19.7 ± 1.8 MPa, comparable to Ar plasma activation. The leakage measurements were performed on Cu/SiO2 damascene comb structures, whereas the bonding validation addresses the dielectric part of the hybrid-bonding interface; Cu–Cu contact and long-term stress testing remain to be verified. This work provides a framework for understanding electric-field-driven surface ionic transport and practical guidelines for contamination control of the dielectric surface in wet-activated Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding.

title: A Rutin–Glycyrrhizic Acid Self-Assembled Nanohydrogel Promotes Early Osteogenic Differentiation Potential and Antioxidant Activity via Synergistic Inhibition of the IL-1β/NF-κB Axis
abstract: Abstract Plant-derived natural compounds have gained increasing attention in biomaterial development due to their intrinsic bioactivity and favorable biocompatibility. The anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and osteogenic properties of rutin and glycyrrhizic acid have rendered them increasingly attractive candidates for therapeutic biomaterial development. However, their poor bioavailability significantly restricts their broad biomedical applications. Inspired by a supramolecular self-assembly strategy, we successfully constructed a rutin–glycyrrhizic acid nanohydrogel (RU–GA). The microstructure and formation mechanism were investigated through experimental characterization and computational simulations. Rutin (RU) and glycyrrhizic acid (GA) self-assemble into a carrier-free hydrogel in aqueous solution via hydrogen bonding and π–π stacking interactions, exhibiting favorable injectability, shapeability, and stability. RU–GA can disperse in water and release rutin–glycyrrhizic acid nanoparticles (RG NPs) with homogeneous particle sizes, while the hydrogel material possesses degradation and sustained-release properties. The bioavailability of RU and GA is synergistically improved through size effects and continuous release. Notably, the RU–GA hydrogel significantly promotes antioxidant activity and early osteogenic differentiation potential relative to the individual monomer components. Bioinformatics analysis further suggested that these bioactivities are associated with IL1B. Il1b knockdown experiments validated that RU and GA may synergistically suppress IL-1β-mediated NF-κB activation, thereby reducing oxidative stress and enhancing early osteogenic differentiation potential. Collectively, the rutin–glycyrrhizic acid nanohydrogel (RU–GA) represents a promising functional biomaterial, providing a strategy for the broad application of natural compounds in biomedical and related fields.

title: Enzyme-Powered Nanomotor as a Mobile Immobilization Carrier for Facilitating the Enzymatic Degradation of Chitin
abstract: Abstract Chitin, the second most abundant biomass after cellulose on earth, can be degraded into chitin oligosaccharides (CHOS), which hold considerable commercial value. However, the sustainable bioconversion of chitin is impeded by its mass transfer limitations and poor accessibility of chitinase to the substrate. Herein, a Janus urease-powered nanomotor (JUNM) was synthesized via a facile approach and employed as an immobilization carrier for chitinase (Chi B) to improve the enzymatic production of CHOS. It was demonstrated that the structural asymmetry of JUNM enabled the asymmetric decomposition of urea, thereby achieving more efficient self-propulsion at low urea concentrations than a symmetric urease-powered nanomotor (UNM). The self-propulsive behavior of the resulting immobilized chitinase nanomotor (Chi B@JUNM) enhanced its enzymatic performance. Compared with the passive counterpart, the enhanced enzyme–substrate contact induced by the autonomous movement and by the substrate adsorption resulting from electrostatic interactions improved the substrate affinity (a 50% decrease in apparent Km) and led to a 53% increase in catalytic efficiency (apparent kcat·Km–1). Moreover, the immobilization of Chi B on JUNM exhibited typical advantages of enhanced stability and reusability. As a result, the final CHOS yield achieved by the self-propelled Chi B@JUNM (with 50 mM urea) was 1.34 and 2.15 times the yield of passive Chi B@JUNM and free Chi B, respectively. Taken together, the reported enzyme-powered nanomotor provided an efficient platform for chitin degradation and paved the way for the design of advanced immobilization carriers to facilitate enzymatic reactions.

title: A Multicyclic Catalytic Network Enabling ROS Amplification, Metabolic Disruption, and Immune Modulation for Antitumor–Antibacterial Therapy
abstract: Abstract Intratumoral bacteria are increasingly recognized as important regulators of tumor progression, immune suppression, and metastasis, whereas current therapeutic strategies remain insufficient to address the coupled tumor–bacteria microenvironment. Here, we report a multicyclic catalytic network (VBC-Net) that integrates alkaline polyoxovanadate with a Bi2WO6–CuSx p–n heterojunction for coordinated antitumor–antibacterial immunotherapy. Unlike conventional single-mechanism nanozymes, VBC-Net establishes interconnected catalytic cycles that sustain ROS amplification, oxygen activation, and glutathione depletion, thereby converting transient catalytic activity into persistent oxidative stress. Simultaneously, the alkaline microenvironment and Bi-associated interference with respiratory-chain-related processes may contribute to metabolic perturbation, coupling oxidative stress with metabolic disruption. VBC-Net is further associated with dendritic-cell maturation, enhanced T-cell infiltration, and pro-inflammatory immune modulation, suggesting remodeling of the tumor–bacteria–immune microenvironment. In murine 4T1 tumor and MRSA-infected models, VBC-Net achieves pronounced tumor suppression, bacterial clearance, reduced metastatic progression, and accelerated wound healing with good biocompatibility. This work establishes a multicyclic catalytic strategy for targeting complex tumor-associated ecosystems and provides a promising framework for antitumor–antibacterial therapy.

title: Molecular Anchoring and Multiscale Porosity Synergize in 3D Printed Polyimide Composites for High-Temperature Thermal Management
abstract: Abstract The large-scale application of energy storage systems such as lithium-ion batteries, which feature high energy density and considerable flammability risks, has created an urgent demand for thermal management materials that offer lightweight construction, high-temperature resistance, efficient insulation, and customizable shaping. Polyimide (PI) is a promising candidate; however, its additive manufacturing is constrained by the high temperatures required for thermal imidization and the severe shrinkage that accompanies this process. To overcome these limitations, herein, an interfacial chemical anchoring strategy is introduced, through which amino-functionalized hollow glass microspheres (HGMs) are covalently integrated into a soluble PI matrix. The achieved composite ink is well-suited for vapor-induced phase separation (VIPS)-assisted direct ink writing (DIW), allowing in situ porosification. The 3D printed constructs thus feature a hierarchical thermal resistance architecture, including macroscopic air gaps from printing, microporous networks derived from phase separation, and hollow HGM cavities, which synergistically suppresses solid conduction, gas convection, and thermal radiation. In addition, the covalently anchored microspheres also serve as crosslinking nodes, enhancing compressive strength. The optimized composites achieve a 35% reduction in density, shrinkage below 5%, a thermal conductivity of 0.048 W·m–1·K–1, and a nearly fourfold improvement in compressive strength. Together, these results demonstrate that the synergy between interfacial chemical anchoring and VIPS-assisted DIW provides a versatile platform for engineering lightweight, high-strength insulation components with tailored geometries for demanding high-temperature applications.

title: Superhydrophobic Self-Cleaning Polyvinyl Alcohol-Based Films for Enhanced Passive Radiative Cooling and Durability
abstract: Abstract Developing sustainable and durable superhydrophobic passive radiative cooling materials is crucial for reducing building energy consumption in a warming world, yet conventional radiative cooling materials often rely on nonrenewable polymeric substrates and fluorosiloxane-based surface modifiers, and present materials have poor durability of superhydrophobicity under harsh conditions, limiting their environmental sustainability and long-term applicability. Herein, we develop a biomass-derived superhydrophobic radiative cooling film by integrating waste straw cellulose with starch and poly(vinyl alcohol) as a renewable film-forming matrix, TiO2 as a solar-reflection filler, and a fluorosiloxane-free surface engineering strategy. The resulting cooling film exhibits a solar reflectance of 76.06% and an infrared emissivity of 96.66% within the atmospheric window. The film achieves an average temperature reduction of 28.2 °C relative to the blank cavity during the test period. Moreover, the superhydrophobic surface imparts excellent self-cleaning capability and enables the film to withstand acid/alkali corrosion, water washing, and prolonged high-temperature treatment (>100 °C for 8 h), demonstrating its robust environmental durability. Beyond passive thermal regulation, the cooling film exhibits an excellent water collection rate of 2476.2 mg cm–2 h–1. The combination of renewable agricultural waste as the structural feedstock, fluorosiloxane-free superhydrophobicity, efficient solar reflection, high infrared emission, and multifunctional environmental stability distinguishes the cooling film from conventional petroleum-based radiative cooling systems. This work provides a sustainable materials-design strategy for converting agricultural waste into multifunctional radiative cooling materials with potential applications in energy-efficient building envelopes and sustainable thermal management.

title: Effective Suppression of Cu+-Migration Assisted Degradation in Perovskite Solar Cells with Cu2O as the Hole Transport Layer
abstract: Abstract Formamidinium-based double-cation perovskite solar cells exhibit rapid performance degradation when the Cu2O hole transport layer is in direct contact with the perovskite. This degradation is attributed to Cu+ migration into the perovskite lattice, causing structural distortion and the formation of CuI and PbI2. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects Cu+ ions even at the antipodal surface of the perovskite, indicating long-range diffusion of the Cu+ ions, probably through grain-boundary migration. To suppress this, a thin film of benzotriazole is introduced at the Cu2O/perovskite interface as a diffusion-blocking layer that also provides mild surface passivation. Adding poly(acrylonitrile-co-methyl acrylate) to the perovskite synthesis solution passivates the grain boundaries and further prevents the migration of Cu+ towards the perovskite. These modifications effectively curb Cu+ migration and its reaction with the perovskite. Consequently, p-i-n perovskite solar cells with the architecture ITO/Cu2O/perovskite/C60/BCP/Ag, incorporating both modifications, exhibit a significant improvement in power conversion efficiency, from ≈4.7 to 14.4%.

title: Pneumatic Rigid-Soft Coupled Finger with Self-Powered Triboelectric Tactile Sensing toward Potential Application in Lunar Exploration
abstract: Abstract Robotic manipulation in future lunar-surface operations and planetary sample-return missions requires end effectors capable of accommodating irregular objects while maintaining reliable tactile feedback under uncertain contact conditions. Motivated by these challenges, we present a terrestrial proof-of-concept of a pneumatic rigid–soft coupled robotic finger integrating structural regulation and self-powered triboelectric tactile sensing. The finger combines rigid skeletons, fiber-constrained pneumatic chambers, and a finger-pad sensing unit to enable compliant deformation, posture regulation, and tactile perception. A flexible single-electrode triboelectric sensor based on a PDMS-MXene composite generates electrical signals through contact electrification and electrostatic induction without external electrical excitation, while pneumatic actuation, signal acquisition, and computational processing require external power. At an input pressure of 140 kPa, the proximal interphalangeal, distal interphalangeal, and metacarpophalangeal regions achieved bending angles of approximately 84°, 76°, and 65°, respectively. The sensor exhibited stable outputs at contact frequencies of 1–10 Hz and a sensitivity of 0.11 V/kPa over 10–120 kPa. Incorporating 6 wt% MXene increased the output voltage by 50.8% compared with pure PDMS. Combined with a convolutional neural network-long short-term memory model, the system achieved classification accuracies of 97.6% for 10 representative laboratory materials and 99.5% for four surface-roughness levels under controlled terrestrial conditions. Grasping experiments further demonstrated compliant manipulation and tactile perception. These results establish the feasibility of the proposed sensing approach under laboratory conditions, while its applicability to planetary geological materials and space environments remains to be validated.

title: Multiscale Intercalation Strategies for Reconstructing Lamellar MXene Membranes
abstract: Abstract Lamellar MXene membranes, constructed by stacking MXene nanosheets to form two-dimensional nanochannels with ultrafast transport and sieving ability, have emerged as a promising platform for molecular and ionic separations as well as osmotic energy harvesting. However, the performance of these MXene membranes is often constrained by swelling-induced unstable nanochannels and monotonous chemistry environments within nanochannels. One of the most effective routes to these challenges lies in the incorporation of functional intercalation matters into the confined nanochannels of MXene, which not only orchestrate interlayer spacing and nanochannel chemistry but also improve stability by forming multiple interactions with neighboring nanosheets. Over the past decade, a series of multiscale intercalation matters have been designed and explored, mainly spanning from ions to small molecules, polymers, and nanomaterials. Despite significant achievements, a timely and comprehensive review that systematically elucidates how various multiscale intercalation matters reconstruct MXene membranes is missing. In this review, we discuss recent advances in intercalation strategies for lamellar MXene membranes, categorized by the chemical nature and dimensionality of the intercalating matters. We underscore their critical roles in modulating both the structural and chemical features of nanochannels, and we systematically analyze the corresponding effects on transport behavior and separation performance. Finally, some key unresolved challenges and future directions are highlighted to guide the design and synthesis of high-performance lamellar MXene membranes.

title: Monolithic Fabrication of Flexible Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Synapses with Bandgap-Engineered Centimeter-Scale SnSe2 van der Waals Layers
abstract: Abstract The transition of bandgap energies in two-dimensional (2D) materials driven by their miniaturization opens up opportunities for emerging device technologies unattainable with conventional approaches. Herein, “all” 2D optoelectronic synapse devices are reported employing the transition characteristics of wafer-scale 2D tin diselenide (SnSe2) layers directly grown on polymeric substrates at a low temperature of 300 °C. Specifically, a significant thickness-dependent reduction in their band energy from 0.8 to 0.25 eV enables a “monolithic” fabrication of flexible device arrays composed of extremely thin active/passive components; i.e., n-type semiconducting 2D channels seamlessly interfaced with heavily doped metallic-like 2D electrodes. These 2D/2D interfaces exhibit reliable Ohmic transports without the need for work function engineering of contact metals as well as well-preserved mechanical deformability. A variety of optoelectronic synaptic properties are demonstrated in the all-2D devices, including deformation-invariant plasticity updates, which are implementable for high-accuracy pattern recognition of artificial neural networks (ANNs). This study suggests new methodologies for integrating the dimensionally tunable electrical properties of near atom-thickness materials into their scalable manufacturability for emergent neuromorphic applications.

title: Template Mineralized, Decellularized Matrix-Alginate-Based Bioink Provides Structural Reinforcement in Caprine Ex Vivo Bone Defect Model
abstract: Abstract Clinical management of critical-sized bone defects (CSDs) remains a significant surgical problem. Current bioinks fail to support initial loading on bone tissue. In this study, goat-derived decellularized matrix (DCM) was used as a template for controlled mineralization, while alginate improved the printability and cellular viability. DCM proteins acted as a natural template for hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal nucleation and growth, mimicking bone nanocomposite chemistry while enhancing structural reinforcement. HA formation on DCM template was visualized by atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis, characteristic phosphate (PO43–) peaks in attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), and the HA-specific (211) diffraction peak in X-ray diffraction (XRD). Mineralized DCM was blended with alginate to formulate printable bioinks. Rheological analysis showed dominant elastic behavior (G′ > G″), shear-thinning flow, and rapid post-shear recovery. Mechanical testing further demonstrated enhanced compressive strength in HA-DCM-alginate constructs. Bioprinting with osteoblast cells demonstrated higher cellular viability in the mineralized ink while enhancing osteogenic differentiation, via both biochemical and biophysical signaling from the mineralized-DCM ink. In an ex vivo defect model, the HA-DCM-alginate system significantly increased the compressive properties of the defect construct, providing immediate structural reinforcement at the defect site. Overall, the current mineralized bioink can provide both mechanical support and bone regeneration and holds promising potential for surgical application.

title: Nanofibrous Thermo-Optical Materials for Spacecraft Passive Thermal Control
abstract: Abstract Passive thermal control is essential for spacecraft operating in extreme extraterrestrial environments, where minimizing solar heat absorption while maximizing thermal radiation is critical for maintaining acceptable onboard temperatures without additional energy consumption. Here, electrospun nanofibrous materials, represented by a polymeric polytetrafluoroethylene:polyethylene oxide (PTFE:PEO) composite and ceramic silica, are introduced as a new class of lightweight spacecraft thermal control materials combining ultrahigh solar reflectance (or ultralow solar absorptance), strong infrared emittance, and environmental durability.
