title: All 3D-Printed Conducting Polymer Hydrogel-Based Soft Surface Electromyography Electrode Array for Noninvasive Fatigue Assessment
abstract: Abstract High-density surface electromyography (sEMG) electrode arrays allow the recording of rich myoelectric signals and provide a useful approach for monitoring exercise-induced muscle fatigue. However, existing sEMG electrode arrays often suffer from mechanical mismatches between conventional rigid electrodes and soft tissues, as well as complex fabrication processes and limited programmability, which severely constrain the rational design and practical application of sEMG electrode arrays. Herein, we successfully fabricate an eight-channel PEDOT:PSS-PVA hydrogel-based soft sEMG electrode array via a multi-material 3D printing. Through systematic rheological characterization of the composite inks and rational design of a printable three-layer electrode architecture, we achieve seamless interfacial integration and integrated sequential fabrication. The as-prepared sEMG electrode array exhibits exceptional softness comparable to that of human soft tissues (Young’s modulus ∼ 10 kPa), low electrochemical impedance (∼22 Ω), and good electrochemical stability. Leveraging these advantageous properties, our sEMG electrode array enables noninvasive sEMG signal recording and monitoring of fatigue-associated sEMG changes with a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR > 20 dB) under various grip forces before and after exercise, and captures sEMG changes associated with fatigue progression during repetitive movements. These results validate the capability of our electrode array for high-quality sEMG monitoring of fatigue-associated electrophysiological features and open up promising avenues for future applications such as scientific athletic training.

title: Crystallinity-Dependent Donor Activation in RF-Sputtered SnO2 Electron-Transport Layers and the Interface-Character Origin of Their Predicted Device-Level Consequences
abstract: Abstract SnO2 is the electron-transport layer (ETL) in record n–i–p perovskite solar cells, grown by chemical bath deposition (CBD) without high-temperature crystallization; whether its crystallinity matters remains unresolved. Here, the same RF-sputtering process on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO), at room temperature or 300 °C, yields a predominantly amorphous or an FTO-templated polycrystalline rutile film. The measured film and interface properties anchor a calibrated TCAD model and a thirteen-parameter Sobol global sensitivity analysis (>33,000 simulations), which, unlike one-factor-at-a-time sweeps, resolves the interactions among parameters explicitly. At the film level, crystallinity governs donor activation: UPS, XPS, and STEM-EDS show that the amorphous film holds more fluorine yet has a Fermi level farther below the conduction band, so shallow donors attributed to substitutional fluorine exist in both films but are active only in the crystalline one. At the device level, however, the predicted gain arises from the crystalline film's interface rather than its doping. The Ag/SnO2 contact is rectifying on the amorphous film and ohmic on the crystalline one, through interface-state de-pinning rather than a band-offset shift. The Sobol analysis ranks the SnO2/perovskite interface trap density first (total-effect index ≈ 0.66). A degenerately doped film could screen such traps, but the amorphous film's rectification rules out that route; its deficit is interfacial. At its trap density (∼1013 cm–2), only deep acceptor-like states pin the Fermi level (acceptor-fraction index ≈ 0.83). The predicted crystallization gain is +5.6 pp (20.5 → 26.1%). FAPbI3 half-stack PL/TRPL supports this (1.35× longer lifetime on the crystalline ETL) and bounds that interface's trap density to ≲1012 cm–2. Crystalline growth is one route to the de-pinned interface that CBD ETLs reach chemically, provided that interface is preserved. The absolute efficiencies are calibrated predictions; the benefit's sign and the lever ranking are robust.

title: Dielectric Mie-Resonant Metasurface Integrated ATR Chip for Spectrally Tunable Surface-Enhanced Infrared Spectroscopy in Aqueous Media
abstract: Abstract Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy provides label-free molecular fingerprints but often lacks sensitivity for trace analysis in aqueous media. Surface-enhanced infrared absorption (SEIRA) spectroscopy amplifies vibrational signals near nanostructured surfaces, yet conventional SEIRA platforms typically require sample drying, preconcentration, or noble metal substrates. Here, we introduce a monolithic all-silicon chip that integrates dielectric Mie-resonant micropillar arrays onto a microattenuated total reflection (µ-ATR) element using a complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible fabrication process. This µ-ATR SEIRA (µ-SEIRA) chip enables SEIRA directly in bulk aqueous media without sample drying, preconcentration, or noble metals. The µ-SEIRA chip provides spectrally tunable field enhancement, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.57 mM for aqueous sodium acetate, a 3.6-fold improvement over a flat silicon reference. Resonance tuning via the micropillar array geometry enables selective enhancement of specific vibrational bands, as demonstrated by the preferential enhancement of the Amide II band (∼1550 cm–1) over the Amide I band (∼1650 cm–1) in bovine serum albumin. The µ-SEIRA chip is low-cost, scalable, and disposable, reducing cross-contamination and throughput limitations associated with reusable ATR crystals for aqueous sample measurements.

title: Geometry-Driven Ultrahigh Current Density Field Emission from Vertically Oriented MXene Film Edge Emitters
abstract: Abstract MXenes are promising cold cathode materials owing to their high electrical conductivity, solution processability, and tunable surface terminations; however, realizing high-current-density field emission from MXene film emitters remains challenging because their planar two-dimensional geometry generally provides limited field concentration and restricts the number of field-activated emission sites. Here, we demonstrate a geometry-driven strategy to achieve high-current-density field emission from vertically oriented MXene film edge emitters. By systematically controlling the film height and inter-electrode gap, the optimized emitter achieves a current density of 5020 mA cm–2 at 1520 V, which is more than an order of magnitude higher than the values reported for previous MXene field emitters. Enhanced performance is not governed by the field enhancement factor alone. Instead, it is enabled by the balance between sufficient local field enhancement and a large effective emission area. Experimental Fowler–Nordheim analysis, emission pattern imaging, and the screening-corrected field-enhancement model indicate that excessive field concentration can promote edge-localized emission and reduce the effective emission area, whereas the optimized geometry enables distributed edge emission with improved stability. These findings establish edge-geometry engineering as a design principle for transforming two-dimensional MXene films into high-current-density cold cathodes for vacuum nanoelectronics.

title: Peptide–DNA Hybrid Selection for Chemical Functionality Recognition across Diverse Material Interfaces
abstract: Abstract Sequence-defined affinity ligands are powerful tools for molecular recognition, yet their selection has largely focused on defined molecular targets rather than shared chemical functionalities. Extending sequence-based recognition to a chemical moiety presents a distinct challenge because the same functionality must be recognized across structurally and chemically diverse molecular and material contexts. Here, we demonstrate that in vitro selection of peptide–DNA hybrids can generate an affinity ligand that recognizes a shared chemical functionality across distinct molecular and material interfaces. Using carboxylates as a model functionality, we selected a peptide–DNA hybrid library against a carboxylated material surface and identified R8rank1, whose enhanced binding depended on the selected DNA sequence functioning within the peptide–DNA hybrid architecture. R8rank1 hybrid preferentially recognized carboxylate-containing polymers with distinct molecular backbones over polymers bearing other functionalities, including an anionic sulfonate-containing polymer, and retained its recognition behavior across chemically distinct gold and silica nanoparticle interfaces presenting surface carboxylates. Fluorescently labeled R8rank1 further distinguished carboxylated from hydroxylated silica nanoparticles with an approximately eightfold difference in fluorescence and exhibited an apparent Kd of approximately 390 nM for the carboxylated surface, whereas the two surfaces were not significantly differentiated by zeta-potential measurements. This affinity-based readout provides chemical-functionality information complementary to conventional surface charge characterization. These findings extend sequence-based affinity selection from defined molecular targets to shared chemical functionalities and establish peptide–DNA hybrids as a selectable molecular recognition platform for identifying chemical functionalities across diverse material interfaces.

title: Electrode-Side Catalytic Regulation Directs Electrolyte Decomposition for Stable Silicon Anodes
abstract: Abstract The electrochemical stability of silicon anodes is critically influenced by the initial decomposition pathways of fluorine-containing electrolyte species, which dictate the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) composition and stability. However, existing strategies primarily rely on electrolyte fluorination or artificial interphases to indirectly regulate SEI chemistry, whereas precise electrode-side regulation of fluorine-containing electrolyte decomposition remains challenging. Herein, a binder-free Co SACs-Si-N/C electrode is developed to direct interfacial reactions through single-atom catalysis. Atomically dispersed Co-N4 sites selectively strengthen PF6– adsorption, modulate the interfacial electronic structure, and steer fluorine-containing electrolyte species toward preferential inorganic decomposition, thereby constructing a compact LiF-rich SEI that suppresses parasitic reactions and stabilizes the silicon/electrolyte interface. As a result, the Co SACs-Si-N/C electrode delivers a reversible capacity of 1128.8 mAh g–1 after 1200 cycles at 1.0 A g–1, while lithium cobalt oxide pouch cells further demonstrate their practical applicability. Machine learning established a quantitative correlation between electrochemical characterization parameters and performance evolution. This work reveals the critical role of electrode-regulated interfacial reaction pathways in governing SEI evolution and provides a catalytic strategy for developing durable silicon-based anodes.

title: Boosting Photocatalytic Performance via Electron Transfer Regulation in Biocomponent Hybrid Heterojunctions
abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of global climate change and the energy crisis, developing efficient and sustainable catalytic technologies is crucial for addressing environmental and energy challenges. Compared to traditional heterojunctions, the incorporation of natural biogenic components holds great potential for overcoming bottlenecks such as complex crystal engineering, insufficient stability, and limited selectivity. This review established an electron transfer regulation framework to guide the construction of biocomponent hybrid heterojunctions for superior photocatalysis. We systematically cover various biogenic components and their derivatives, from small molecules, conjugated polymers, and supramolecular assemblies, to three-dimensional networks and crystal frameworks such as metal–organic frameworks and covalent-organic frameworks. Based on in-depth mechanistic analysis, this review demonstrates how these biogenic components modulate band engineering, charge transfer kinetics, substrate utilization, and defect passivation, which collectively achieve sequential optimization across the entire charge-carrier lifecycle—from generation and transport to surface reaction and long-term stability. Importantly, all of these directly linked to enhanced photocatalytic performance in H2 evolution, CO2 reduction, H2O2 generation, and pollutant degradation. In addition to conventional band engineering, novel mechanisms such as exciton behavior modulation and conjugated continuity regulation are discussed. This framework transforms empirical material design into predictable catalysis optimization, aiming to accelerate the development of high-performance biocomponent hybrid heterojunctions.

title: Selenium-Integrated MoO3 Composite Cathode for Rechargeable Magnesium Batteries
abstract: Abstract Owing to their high volumetric capacity, potential for low-dendrite metal deposition, and abundance of natural magnesium, rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) have garnered significant interest as potential substitutes for lithium-based systems. Nevertheless, sluggish Mg2+ diffusion and the polyselenide shuttle effect in selenium-based cathodes continue to restrict their practicality. In this work, a Se-MoO3 composite cathode was prepared by solvothermal synthesis of a MoSe2 precursor followed by annealing in air. Compact MoSe2 nanosheets were annealed to create an open hierarchical Se-MoO3 architecture composed of vertically oriented nanosheets associated with MoO3 nanoribbons. The Se-MoO3 cathode delivers 312 mAh g–1 at cycle 80 at 200 mA g–1. At 500 mA g–1, the capacity reaches 237 mAh g–1 at cycle 79 and decreases to 76.8 mAh g–1 at cycle 500. Ex situ measurements reveal reversible changes in the Mo and Se chemical states during cycling, supporting the participation of both components in charge storage. Although the close association between the Se-containing phase and MoO3 may influence the electrochemical response, the present data do not directly establish interface-specific polyselenide adsorption or catalytic conversion. Overall, this work emphasizes compositional and architectural modification as a viable approach for enhanced magnesium-ion storage.

title: D-A-D Engineered Electrochromic Coordination Metallopolymers for Smart Windows, Energy Storage, and Wearables
abstract: Abstract Electrochromic coordination metallopolymers featuring multi-redox centers and structural versatility offer great potential for smart windows and glazing, yet they are hampered in practical application owing to the intrinsic trade-off between optical modulation and charge storage. Herein, we introduce a benzothiadiazole acceptor to construct a donor–acceptor–donor architecture that enhances intramolecular charge transfer and enables intervalence charge transfer, narrowing the bandgap and improving near-infrared electrochromism and capacitance. The resulting BT-CMP//V2O5 device exhibits large optical contrast (ΔT > 50%), fast switching (1.7/3.8 s), and high coloration efficiency (>300 cm2·C–1), enabling efficient photothermal modulation with an annual energy saving of 155.19 MJ·m–2. The D-A-D architecture facilitates rapid and complete charge separation, endowing the polymer with superior energy storage performance, including a high areal capacitance of 38.24 mF·cm–2. Furthermore, flexible prototypes exhibit EC and energy storage, maintain stable performance after 100 bending cycles. This D-A-D strategy provides a versatile platform to overcome the intrinsic trade-off of electrochromic materials, paving the way for high-performance electrochromic energy storage devices.

title: Quantitative Solvation Scale for Lithium Battery Electrolytes
abstract: Abstract Understanding electrolyte solvation is vital for developing advanced lithium batteries, as solvation structures dictate interfacial chemistry and performance. This study evaluates the reliability of conventional 1D NMR techniques (1H, 7Li, 19F, and 13C) for probing lithium solvation. We demonstrate that absolute chemical shifts often correlate poorly with solvating ability, leading to misleading interpretations—a finding cross-validated by FTIR and DOSY. We identify that the change in chemical shift (Δδ) from 13C NMR serves as a robust descriptor, provided that the probe solvent’s solvating ability matches the system. To overcome single-probe limitations, we introduce a multiprobe strategy using ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), trifluoroethyl methyl carbonate (FEMC), and propylene carbonate (PC). This approach establishes a quantitative solvation scale across weak, intermediate, and strong solvating regimes. The resulting scale shows strong linear correlations with coordination ratios and solvating power, enabling precise linear free-energy relationships. We demonstrate the practical utility of this framework by accurately predicting lithium nitrate solubility and guiding electrolyte design. Ultimately, this work provides a reliable, broadly applicable methodology for advancing next-generation battery electrolytes. Most importantly, this work provides a lithium solvating strength series, offering a highly useful tool for researchers to compare common solvents.

title: Potential-Dependent Hydricities and Bond Dissociation Free Energies of Metal Surface Hydrides
abstract: Abstract Recent experimental studies demonstrate that the thermodynamic hydricity of surface-bound intermediates is continuously tunable via electrical polarization. Canonical density functional theory relies on constant-charge models that fail to capture this potential-dependent polarization at the electrified solid-liquid interface. This work implements grand-canonical density functional theory (GC-DFT) to compute the surface hydricity, bond dissociation free energy (BDFE), and acidity of chemisorbed hydrogen across transition metal facets. Assuming an outer-sphere transfer isolates the intrinsic hydrogen-donating capacity of the active site. By explicitly controlling the system Fermi level, we demonstrate that surface hydricity exhibits a universal linear dependence on applied cathodic bias across all evaluated facets. In contrast, the potential dependence of the homolytic BDFE is strictly governed by material identity: platinum maintains a relatively static bond strength, while silver and copper exhibit potential-induced bond stabilization. The computed hydricity slopes for Pt facets quantitatively reproduce the experimentally measured polarization-dependent hydride-transfer sensitivity. Coordination geometry dictates the baseline donor capacity, with lower coordination atop sites on Ag and Cu functioning as significantly stronger hydride donors. Adlayer saturation perturbs the thermodynamic values in a metal-dependent manner, weakening hydride donation on silver but strengthening it on copper. However, at the two coverages examined, it does not substantially alter the voltage sensitivity of the thermodynamic properties. Evaluating voltage-dependent hydricity provides a thermodynamic framework for characterizing the intrinsic hydride- or hydrogen-donating ability of electrified solid-liquid interfaces.

title: Structural Insights into Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers after Long-Term Operation Using Advanced 3D Focused Ion Beam–Scanning Electron Microscopy Tomography
abstract: Abstract Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are key to sustainable hydrogen production, but their long-term performance is limited by degradation, particularly in the membrane electrode assembly (MEA), which remains a barrier to commercial viability. Moreover, the need for corrosion-resistant materials and the intricate fabrication of bipolar plates and porous transport layers (PTLs) further impede large-scale deployment and account for a major share of the stack cost. Because lifetime and replacement costs are strongly influenced by the local microstructure and contact conditions, especially at the anode/PTL interface, a multiscale characterization approach combining 3D focused ion beam–scanning electron microscopy (FIB–SEM) with time-of-flight mass spectrometry is used to investigate degradation in an MEA after several thousand hours of operation under industrially relevant conditions. The 3D reconstruction and ppm-level chemical mapping show that local contact heterogeneities at welds in an expanded-metal mesh PTL act as degradation hotspots. At these sites, intensified catalyst utilization accelerates iridium dissolution, driving iridium migration and deposition as extended filaments into the membrane. Concurrently, membrane voids are formed beneath these sites, accompanied by iron contamination detected at both contact types. In contrast, general contact regions mainly show a thin redeposition layer without voids or filaments. These findings provide a mechanistic framework that links local contact conditions and microstructural heterogeneities to coupled catalyst and membrane degradation, supporting design rules for improved PEMWE durability.

title: Controllable Synthesis of Porous Core–Shell NiCo Bimetallic Selenides for High-Performance Supercapacitors
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic framework (MOF)-derived electrode materials suffer from poor conductivity and structural instability. Herein, a porous core–shell NiCo bimetallic selenide (NiCo PBA–Se) is synthesized via a multistep liquid-phase transformation followed by low-temperature selenization. A Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-67 (ZIF-67) shell is first epitaxially grown on a Ni-MOF core to construct a core–shell MOF hybrid as the precursor for the preparation of subsequent electrode materials. Unlike conventional methods that convert only the outer MOF layer, the precisely controlled ion-exchange process converts both the inner Ni-MOF and outer ZIF-67 into a NiCo-PBA precursor while preserving the core–shell spherical morphology. Gas-phase selenization at 350 °C yields the target product, which retains a three-dimensional porous spherical architecture composed of stacked ultrathin nanosheets. Ni and Co are uniformly incorporated into the selenide lattice, forming a single-phase (Ni, Co)Se2 solid solution that shortens ion transport paths and increases active sites. Kinetic analysis reveals a synergistic combination of diffusion-controlled and capacitance-controlled charge storage, enabling rapid charge/discharge. In three-electrode tests, NiCo PBA–Se delivers a specific capacitance of 1642 F·g–1 (738.9 C·g–1) at 1 A·g–1. The assembled asymmetric supercapacitor achieves an energy density of 42.52 Wh·kg–1 at 775 W·kg–1 and powers an electronic timer for 20 min. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the MOF-on-MOF strategy with full conversion of both core and shell and simultaneous maintenance of the core–shell structure for constructing high-performance multimetal selenides.

title: Depth-Resolved Magnetic Reversal of La0.7Sr0.3Mn1– x Ru x O3-Based Synthetic Antiferromagnets
abstract: Abstract Synthetic antiferromagnets based on transition metal oxides provide a versatile platform for engineering magnetic functionalities beyond those of conventional metallic systems. However, the microscopic pathways by which their magnetization reverses remain difficult to determine because conventional magnetic measurements cannot resolve the layer-specific magnetic configurations that emerge during switching. Here, we combine polarized neutron reflectometry, magnetometry, magnetotransport, and an extended Stoner–Wohlfarth model to investigate the magnetization reversal mechanisms in epitaxial La0.7Sr0.3Mn1–xRuxO3/LaNiO3 multilayers. Depth-resolved polarized neutron reflectometry reveals non-collinear magnetic configurations that are hidden from macroscopic probes and identifies the competition between tilted magnetic anisotropy and comparable bilinear and biquadratic interlayer exchange interactions as the origin of the observed behavior. Depending on the magnetic-field orientation, the system undergoes either abrupt switching between magnetic fan and synthetic antiferromagnetic states or a gradual opening of the magnetic fan. Our results establish the intimate connection between magnetic anisotropy, interlayer exchange, and reversal dynamics in oxide synthetic antiferromagnets, revealing correlated oxides as a powerful platform for tuning the balance between competing interactions and engineering tailored magnetic reversal pathways and functionalities.

title: Alkali-Assisted MOCVD Growth of Polycrystalline MoS2 with Micrometer-Scale Domains on Soda-Lime Glass
abstract: Abstract Achieving large-scale, uniform MoS2 films with reduced grain boundary density remains a central challenge for scalable device applications. Previous studies have reported that alkali-assisted growth promotes lateral domain expansion through eutectic intermediate formation. Here, metal–organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) of MoS2 on commercial soda-lime glass is investigated. The intrinsic alkali content of soda-lime glass provides a uniform supply across the substrate, while partial surface softening at growth temperature facilitates the incorporation of Mo species within the near-surface region of the glass. The systematic variation of precursor flow conditions enables controlled modulation of nucleation density and domain size while suppressing graphitic carbon co-deposition arising from precursor ligand pyrolysis. High-quality polycrystalline MoS2 with lateral grain sizes ranging from ∼500 nm to 1.5 μm is achieved as uniform, coalesced centimeter-scale films, demonstrating the scalability of this method. Substrate roughness and wafer-to-wafer variability are key factors governing nucleation, highlighting opportunities for substrate optimization. To correlate the material properties with device performance, the films are wet-transferred and integrated into bottom-gated, top-contact field-effect transistors featuring either non-interdigitated or interdigitated source-drain electrodes. The devices exhibit on/off current ratios up to ∼107 and mobilities of ∼8 cm2 V–1 s–1. Overall, this work demonstrates an accessible and scalable route for the growth of electronic-grade polycrystalline MoS2 on soda-lime glass substrates.

title: Interfacial Solvent Engineering Enables Hydrothermally Stable MXene Heterostructures for Printed Wearable Electronics
abstract: Abstract Water-induced degradation of MXene during hydrothermal synthesis severely limits the construction of MXene-based heterostructures for further applications. Herein, an interfacial solvent-engineering strategy was developed to stabilize MXene under harsh hydrothermal conditions. Solvents with a stronger affinity for reactive Ti sites than water can preferentially adsorb at these sites. This competitive adsorption limits direct water–Ti contact and thereby suppresses subsequent MXene oxidation. DFT calculations were used to screen candidate solvents and support the proposed competitive adsorption mechanism, while the experimental results broadly followed the predicted trend. Deoxygenation experiments further supported the dominant role of water in MXene degradation. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that preferential interfacial enrichment of DMF persists at 453 K despite enhanced thermal motion. In a 50 vol % DMF/H2O system, the MXene framework remained well preserved even under prolonged or higher-temperature hydrothermal treatment. This regulated solvent environment enabled the in situ growth of 1T-MoS2 on the preserved MXene framework. The conductive MXene framework and abundant active sites of 1T-MoS2 led to enhanced electrochemical performance. The resulting composite was further processed into printed microsupercapacitors and pressure sensors, which were integrated into a self-powered pressure-sensing system. This work establishes interfacial solvent engineering as an effective route to hydrothermally stable MXene heterostructures for printed wearable electronics.

title: Synergistic Effect of Hybrid Polarized Spin Currents Enables Sub-Nanosecond and Energy-Efficient Field-Free Switching on a Wafer-Scale Platform
abstract: Abstract Spin–orbit torque magnetoresistive random access memory (SOT-MRAM) exhibits intrinsic potential for next-generation magnetic memory, whereas robust wafer-level field-free switching (FFS) of nanosized perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (pMTJ) remains a critical challenge for practical applications. Here, we present a robust FFS of 90 nm pMTJs on 300 mm wafers driven by the synergistic effect of y- and z-polarized spin currents generated at the antiferromagnetic (AFM)/nonmagnetic (NM) interface. Experimental results demonstrate that an appropriate combination of both y- and z-spin polarizations is able to significantly improve the FFS performance. 90 nm pMTJ arrays are fabricated on 300 mm wafers, where a mean tunnel magnetoresistance ratio (TMR) of 140%, an endurance of exceeding 1012 cycles, and a robust field-free SOT switching at sub-nanosecond (down to 0.2 ns) are simultaneously achieved. Robust FFS is observed at temperature up to 100 °C, and the switching polarity remains unchanged after 1T magnetic field disturbance. With the assistance of the voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) effect, the switching current density is reduced by 20% and the switching energy can be as low as 0.35 pJ/bit. This work paves the way for SOT-MRAM toward commercialization.

title: In Memoriam: Professor T. Randall Lee, a Distinguished Professor and a Dedicated Mentor with an Impactful Legacy
Rational Synthesis of Sulfonic Acid-Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Capture of Trace Strontium in Natural Mineral Water
abstract: Abstract As a typical long-lived radionuclide, strontium-90 (90Sr) possesses persistent radiological hazards and exhibits high migratory and diffusive behaviors in groundwater. However, the development of adsorbents for the efficient and highly selective capture of trace Sr(II) remains a great challenge. In this study, covalent organic frameworks (COFs, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H) with different numbers of sulfonic acid groups were rationally synthesized and applied for capturing Sr(II). The introduction of sulfonic acid groups onto TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H endowed them with high adsorption capacities of 136.4 and 68.3 mg g–1 toward Sr(II), which were 12-fold and 6-fold higher than that of TpPa without sulfonic acid groups, respectively. Meanwhile, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H exhibited fast adsorption kinetics, capturing 99% of Sr(II) within 3 and 10 min, respectively. In addition, TpPa-2SO3H also exhibited high selectivity, excellent anti-interference performance, and regeneration ability without high calcium backgrounds. Characterizations and theoretical calculations demonstrated that sulfonic acid groups in TpPa-2SO3H promoted Sr(II) capture through strong ion-exchange interaction. TpPa-2SO3H was further applied to extract trace Sr(II) in natural Sr-containing mineral water samples. The results showed that the extraction efficiency for Sr(II) exceeded 95% within 5 min. Furthermore, the selectivity for Sr(II) was investigated by the distribution coefficients (Kd), and the Kd was 5.6 × 104 mL g–1 for TpPa-2SO3H toward Sr(II), approximately 400 times higher than those of Na(I) and K(I), respectively. This work not only developed a promising strategy to extract trace Sr(II) from real samples but also broadened the application of COFs in separation science.

title: Ultrasound-Responsive Iron-Barium Titanate Schottky Heterojunction-Embedded Hydrogel Accelerates Burn Wound Healing through Bidirectional Hydrogen-Piezocatalytic Redox Modulation
abstract: Abstract Burn wound healing is regulated by a spatiotemporal redox hierarchy, where early reactive oxygen species (ROS) overload drives inflammation, while late ROS deficiency hinders regeneration. Programming this bidirectional sequence requires time-phased, counter-directional ROS control. Herein, we report a nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates hydrogen therapy with piezocatalytic therapy, enabling on-demand redox programming across the entire healing cascade. The system constructs a metal-semiconductor Schottky heterojunction derived from the in situ reduction of Fe2+ within the mesopores of barium titanate. The mesoporous confinement and interfacial coupling program the hydrolysis of nanoscale zero-valent iron for sustained, early-stage hydrogen delivery to scavenge toxic ROS, while the established Schottky barrier efficiently suppresses charge recombination, thereby executing ultrasound-triggered piezoelectric polarization and charge separation for on-demand ROS generation in later-stage pro-regenerative signaling. Embedded within a polyacrylamide/carboxymethyl chitosan double-network hydrogel with inherent antibacterial activity, the resulting system exhibits superior antioxidant capacity and piezocatalytic responsivity, as well as promotion of fibroblast migration, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage polarization. In a mouse burn model, this redox-programmable platform orchestrates phased healing, attenuating early inflammation, sustaining neovascularization, and suppressing late fibrosis, achieving accelerated wound closure. Collectively, this work establishes a redox programming paradigm via heterojunction catalysis, coupling spatiotemporal ROS scavenging and generation for dynamic tissue regeneration.

title: Ionic Liquids and Deep Eutectic Solvents as Functional Interfacial Phases in Membrane-Based Separations
abstract: Abstract In this Spotlight on Applications, we describe our progress in developing membrane-based separation processes in which ionic liquids (ILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DESs) act as functional interfacial phases rather than merely as alternative solvents or extractants. Starting from stability limitations identified in supported ionic liquid membranes, our work evolved toward architectures in which polymeric materials selectively contact, confine, distribute, or stabilize ionic and eutectic liquid phases. We organize these contributions according to the location and function of the active interface: external polymer–ionic liquid interfaces in dense membrane systems; localized ionic or eutectic phases confined within multilayer membrane architectures; distributed polymer–DES domains in dense hybrid membranes; membrane-stabilized contact with mobile immiscible liquid phases; and liquid–vapor–membrane interfaces in ionic-liquid-driven osmotic distillation. Each architecture builds on an established membrane-process category – perstraction, coated liquid membranes, polymer inclusion membranes, membrane contactors, and osmotic distillation – and is distinguished by the location, flow regime, and function of the ionic or eutectic phase. These configurations were applied to fermentation-product recovery, selective separation of target molecules, ethanol dehydration, food concentration, and water recovery from saline streams. Across these applications, performance emerged from the synergistic coupling of polymer sorption and diffusion, liquid-phase affinity, wetting, morphology, interfacial stability, and resistance distribution. COSMO-RS provided a complementary progression from solute–ionic-liquid screening to direct polymer screening and, subsequently, to thermodynamic interpretation of hybrid polymer–eutectic membrane environments. Collectively, these studies indicate that the polymer, ionic or eutectic phase, solute, interface, operating mode, and membrane architecture should be designed as an integrated interfacial system.

title: Dual Conical Fibers for Controllable Liquid Transfer
abstract: Abstract Solution processes, especially those using open systems, have shown advantages of mild conditions, cost-effectiveness, and broad substrate compatibility in making micro-patterned functional films of optoelectronic devices. Owing to the extreme dynamics of liquids, finely controlling liquid transfer remains largely unsolved, particularly across dimensions from μm- to cm-scale. Here, we propose a model structure of dual conical fibers (dual-CFs) that enables liquid transfer to proceed in a well-controllable manner for micro-patterning. The critical structural parameters for fully holding liquid within dual-CFs are clarified, and quantitative correlations between fiber topology and steady liquid transfer are established. The dual-parallel-fibrous structure, representing the minimum number of CFs for the structure model, helps suppress Plateau–Rayleigh instability by virtue of the confined noncircular cross-sectional liquid film; while the conical structure enables effectively holding liquid, without any leakage during the transfer process, due to the as-generated Laplace pressure difference. The dual-CFs benefit from minimizing the rupture energy of the liquid film by the minimal cross-sectional area confined at the tips, which leads to finely anchoring the three-phase contact line. As a synergistic consequence, liquid can be transferred onto substrates in a controllable manner, resulting in micro-patterns with well-defined profiles. More importantly, the model structure of dual-CFs can be programmably arranged into multi-conical fiber arrays, by which direct-writing micro-patterns from μm-scale microlines to cm-scale uniform films can be realized. The direct-writing strategy is applicable for making functional micro-patterns, offering inspiration for micro-patterning liquid materials using fibrous open systems.

title: A Biomimetic Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoreactor Reshapes ROS Homeostasis and Activates STING Pathway for Synergistic Chemodynamic–Immunotherapy
abstract: Abstract The combination of chemodynamic therapy (CDT) and immunotherapy offers a promising therapeutic paradigm for advanced cancer treatment, yet its translation is largely hindered by inadequate intratumoral reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and the lack of a robust link between ROS-induced cytotoxicity and durable immune activation. To address these challenges, we herein engineer a multifunctional biomimetic nanoplatform (ZMGM) by encapsulating Mn2+ and glucose oxidase (GOX) within zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8), followed by surface functionalization with 4T1 breast cancer cell membranes. This design integrates three synergistic functions: (1) GOX depletes glucose and generates hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) within the acidic tumor microenvironment; (2) the produced H2O2 fuels the Mn2+-mediated Fenton-like reaction to amplify ROS production; and (3) Mn2+ simultaneously serves as a potent stimulator of interferon genes (STING) agonist, triggering type-I interferon responses and promoting dendritic cell maturation. Meanwhile, the homologous cancer cell membrane coating endows ZMGM with specific tumor homing and enhanced tumor localization. Both in vitro and in vivo findings demonstrate that ZMGM not only efficiently eradicates primary tumors but also induces a systemic antitumor immune response, characterized by increased CD8+ T cell infiltration, that effectively suppresses distant metastatic lesions. Notably, the synergistic CDT–STING immunotherapy achieves a primary tumor inhibition rate of 84.22% without obvious systemic toxicity. This work provides a paradigm for rationally designing a single nanoplatform that bridges ROS-mediated cell killing and innate immune activation, offering a promising avenue for combating metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.

title: Porous-Architectured Composite for Fully 3D-Printed Biodegradable Soft Electronics
abstract: Abstract Biodegradable electronics offer the promise of implantable devices that disappear after use, reducing the need for surgical removal and mitigating chronic inflammatory responses. Achieving both tissue-level mechanical softness and sufficient electrical conductivity is critical for bioelectronics. Composite materials provide a versatile platform to satisfy these electrical and mechanical requirements, while 3D printing allows precise and customizable fabrication of complex and multi-material structures. However, in fully biodegradable composites, limited material options restrict simultaneous optimization of mechanical and electrical properties. Here, we introduce engineered internal porosity into a biodegradable electronic composite to achieve softer mechanical properties while maintaining electrical performance. In metal-polymer composites, a porous matrix promotes filler aggregation, forming a percolating conductive network at a lower filler loading compared to non-porous counterparts, thereby reducing stiffness. Engineered porosity within the printed structure reduces its elastic modulus by orders of magnitude and accelerates degradation. We also demonstrate multi-material 3D printing of porosity-programmed electronic inks for printed circuit boards and sensors applications. This structural strategy can be extended to other biodegradable filler-binder systems, thereby expanding the material palette for next-generation transient electronics.

title: Cellulose-Derived Water-Free, Anti-Freezing, and Self-Initiated Ionogel for Flexible Wearable Electronics
abstract: Abstract The growing demand for sustainable flexible electronics has positioned cellulose as a promising candidate, yet its efficient dissolution and functionalization remain challenging due to its highly crystalline structure and strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding. While a wide variety of cellulose dissolution systems have been reported in the literature, most systems still depend on toxic initiators or complex processes. Herein, we report a sunlight-driven, initiator-free green synthesis of cellulose-based ionogels that enables direct cellulose dissolution and in situ photopolymerization, which provides a facile and sustainable route to anti-freezing ionogels via the direct in situ polymerization of ionogel precursors without initiators or crosslinkers. Notably, the incorporation of cellulose, along with the intrinsic properties of the 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride ([Bmim]Cl) and ethylene glycol (EG) significantly enhanced the mechanical properties of the conductive ionogel, which exhibited outstanding mechanical performance (fracture strain of 935%, fracture stress of 166.5 kPa), robust adhesive properties (1.48 MPa), excellent conductivity (0.028 mS·cm–1) and wide work temperature range (–20∼60 °C). These properties enabled the ionogel to function not only as a wearable strain sensor for motion detection but also as a self-powered controller for operating a remote-controlled car via human-computer interaction. This work provides a versatile and sustainable strategy for fabricating high-performance cellulose ionogels, paving the high value-added way for future soft electronic systems with multifunctional integration.

title: Antiferroelectric hafnia down to the 2D limit
abstract: Antiferroelectricity is a material property characterized by alternating electric dipoles spontaneously ordered in antiparallel directions. Antiferroelectrics are promising for energy storage, solid-state cooling, and memory technologies; however, these materials are scarce, and their scalability remains largely unexplored. In this work, we demonstrated that single-crystalline hafnia, a lead-free complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)–compatible material, exhibits antiferroelectricity under compressive-strain conditions. We observed antiparallel sublattice polarization and stable double hysteresis in single-crystalline (111)-oriented epitaxial lanthanum (La)–doped hafnia films grown on yttrium-stabilized zirconia and showed that the antipolar orthorhombic phase of hafnia adheres to the Kittel model of antiferroelectricity. Compressive strain strengthens the orthorhombic order in thinner La-doped hafnia films, achieving a very high ordering temperature of 850°C in the two-dimensional limit, highlighting hafnia’s potential for advanced antiferroelectric devices.

title: Tracking danger on the peaks
abstract: The Earth is warming, but not all regions are warming equally. In high mountain areas, temperatures are generally increasing by 1.5 to 2 times the global average, sometimes with devastating consequences. A small or gradual change in the mountain cryosphere—perhaps progressive thawing of frozen ground or a flood from a small glacial lake—can suddenly turn into a cascade of catastrophes with enormous ramifications. Monitoring systems for the cryosphere in high mountain areas have traditionally been designed to look at individual components and changes. What are the temperature and depth of the permafrost, or how much area is covered by snow, and what is the related avalanche danger? Many of the monitoring and warning systems were designed for historical patterns of snowfall or rainfall, and a river gauge may no longer be adequate if there is greater flow in the rainy season, or increased sediment that could damage the gauge.

title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
abstract: Submarine landslides threaten seabed infrastructure and trigger the transport of globally important amounts of sediment, carbon, and pollutants to deep-sea environments. However, fully submarine landslides have never been directly monitored in nature. Past hypotheses for their failure mechanism and dynamics therefore remain unvalidated for natural settings, including that prolonged upslope-migrating failures (breaching) occur in sandy seafloor environments. In this work, we present direct underwater monitoring of fully submarine landslides at Homathko Delta in western Canada that retrogress slowly upslope, indicating breaching-type failure. Their prolonged rather than instantaneous nature has important implications for the stress that seabed structures must be designed to withstand. Prolonged landslides also initiate sustained sediment flows (turbidity currents) that efficiently transport sediment, carbon, and pollutants further offshore.

title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: Strongly correlated and topological phases in moiré materials are exquisitely sensitive to lattice geometry at both atomic and superlattice length scales. Twist angle, pressure, and strain directly modify the lattice and thus act as highly effective tuning parameters. Here, we examined electrical transport in twisted bilayer graphene subjected to continuous uniaxial strain. Near the magic angle (≈1.1°), devices exhibited a pronounced elastoresistance that depended on band filling and temperature, with a gauge factor more than two orders of magnitude larger than that of conventional metals. In selected doping regimes, the elastoresistance exhibited a Curie-Weiss–like temperature divergence. We discuss possible microscopic origins, including nematic fluctuations and enhanced electronic entropy from fluctuating isospin moments. Our work establishes uniaxial strain as a versatile probe of correlated physics in a moiré material.

title: A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment
abstract: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. We analyzed 854,911 cells from 159 patients by single cell RNA sequencing and 39 samples by spatial transcriptomics, which identified 9 cell types and 60 cell states. Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

title: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space
abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

title: Leading with humility
Differentiation of stem-like CD4 + T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer
abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

title: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak
abstract: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.

title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability
abstract: Whether genomic data can be used to effectively predict adaptation in natural populations is unknown. Here, we tested the efficacy of genomic prediction of complex trait evolution by monitoring genome-wide allele frequencies and pigmentation variation in genetically diverse populations of Drosophila melanogaster during evolution in both field mesocosms and a controlled, lab-based setting. At two points during trait evolution, we produced a high-powered, well-resolved genotype-phenotype map that exhibited marked stability across independent populations. Although we were able to use this map to correctly infer the direction of pigmentation evolution in both the lab and field settings, the particular loci responding to selection were largely unpredictable based on the direction of trait evolution itself. Our results hold implications for the promise, and limitations, of genomic prediction.

title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants
abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

title: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome outbreak linked to cruise ship travel in April–May 2026
abstract: In April 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. ANDV genome sequences were obtained for 10 of the 13 identified cases during a cross-country investigation established to share initial raw data for joint analysis with reciprocal quality control. The genomic data, symptom onsets, and plausible contact patterns strongly support a tightly linked outbreak cluster compatible with a single or very few zoonotic spillover events prior to embarkment followed by human-to-human transmission onboard. The outbreak represents the international displacement of a virus already known to be capable, under specific conditions, to transmit among humans, and does not suggest emergence of a unusual viral strain.

title: Carbon dioxide and amorphous water ices in the debris disk around β Pictoris
abstract: The star β Pictoris is orbited by a dusty debris disk, within which planet formation is occurring. The outer disk is sufficiently far from the star that volatile molecules are expected to freeze into solid ices. We observed the β Pictoris disk in the near-infrared using the James Webb Space Telescope. The spectrum shows features due to amorphous water ice (2 ) ice in both the 12 CO 2 and 13 CO 2 isotopologues. We infer that the CO 2 ice is intimately mixed with the water ice at a ratio of 1:10. This implies that the ices formed in cold conditions, likely in the interstellar medium. Frequent collisions within the debris disk are required to explain the observed uniform distribution of icy dust grains.

The genetic landscape of canine tumors: Insights from the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA)
abstract: The Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA, https://caninecancergenomeatlas.org/ ) is an open, accessible comparative oncology resource that harmonizes whole-exome data across 10 canine tumor histotypes. It aggregates 667 tumor-normal pairs with curated single-nucleotide variants, insertions and deletions, structural variants, and copy number aberrations. Cohort-depth stratification distinguished primary, exploratory, and descriptive analyses. Selection analyses identified 39 cancer drivers, including recurrent TP53 , PIK3CA , PTEN , SETD2 , MAP3K14 , and FAT4 alterations; copy number events included MYC amplifications and PTEN deletions. Direct comparison with matched human cancers revealed conserved and species-enriched oncogenic mechanisms, pathways, and therapeutic contexts. The CCGA standardizes alignment, variant calling, and annotation through consensus pipelines and provides downloadable data and interactive analyses. This reusable framework advances precision veterinary oncology and strengthens translational bridges to human cancer, supporting comparative and translational research.

title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca 2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes
abstract: Lysosomal Ca 2+ release from acidic stores is critical for lysosomal function, yet the molecular identity of the Ca 2+ uptake conduit has remained elusive. We used a Ca 2+ -imaging–based genetic screen of the lysosomal membrane proteome to identify TMEM184 family proteins as lysosomal Ca 2+ transporters (LyCaTs) essential for Ca 2+ uptake and refilling. TMEM184 selectively transported Ca 2+ while excluding monovalent cations. Loss of TMEM184B/C depleted lysosomal Ca 2+ stores, diminished Ca 2+ release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human TMEM184B mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca 2+ transport, and Tmem184b -deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca 2+ uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.

title: EDITOR’S NOTE on the Research Article “Mucus enhances gut homeostasis and oral tolerance by delivering immunoregulatory signals”
Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids
abstract: Electron hydrodynamics is an emerging framework that describes dynamics of interacting electron systems as conventional fluids. Although evidence for hydrodynamic-like transport has been reported in a variety of two-dimensional materials, precise quantitative measurement of the core parameter, electron viscosity, remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate that magnetoresistance in Corbino-shaped graphene devices offers a simultaneous ohmmeter and viscosometer capability, allowing us to disentangle the individual ohmic and viscous contributions to transport, even near viscous-ohmic crossover. In both monolayer and bilayer graphene, the effective electron-electron scattering rate scales linearly with temperature, deviating markedly from the T 2 dependence expected in conventional Fermi liquids. Instead, it is consistent with a recently identified tomographic fluid regime, theoretically predicted to be generic for two-dimensional electron systems.

title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly
abstract: Innate immune systems of living organisms are essential for host defense. Central to these systems is the Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, an evolutionarily conserved module. From antiphage systems in prokaryotes to innate immune systems in plants, TIR domains have catalytic activity. However, TIR domains within animal innate immune receptors, such as Toll-like receptors (TLRs), have been considered as scaffolds for adaptor recruitment. We report that the TLR4 TIR domain possesses an allosterically activated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) hydrolase (NADase) activity that operates in a single-turnover manner. Its product, adenosine diphosphate ribose, is not released but entrapped as a “molecular glue,” stabilizing a composite catalytic pocket with adaptor TIR domain–containing adaptor protein (TIRAP) to nucleate signalosome assembly. This “produce-and-trap” mechanism represents a signaling mode that integrates enzymatic activity with adaptor function to drive downstream signaling.

title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
abstract: After the African origin of Homo sapiens , multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on ‘Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi ), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.

title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs
abstract: Nitrate pollution is widely perceived as a signature of human inputs. Here we show, with machine-learning reconstructed global maps, that climate aridity is also a dominant driver, systematically elevating nitrate concentrations across land-use gradients and creating unexpected hotspots beyond major agricultural and urban centers. Across ~2.9 million river segments worldwide, nitrate concentrations exceed ecological and health thresholds across ~33 and 2% of global land area, affecting ~5.6 billion (73%) and 0.5 billion (6%) people, respectively. Ecological threshold exceedance occurs mostly in headwaters, and about half of the health threshold exceedance occurs in middle-income countries and sparsely populated landscapes. These findings cast nitrate pollution as an aridity-amplified risk, suggesting that aridification may increase nitrate exposure even without additional human inputs. They call for regulatory standards that reflect risks across broad concentration ranges.

title: Atmospheric O 2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990
abstract: The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen (O 2 ) and CO 2 observations, we find that the ocean carbon sink increased by 0.63 ± 0.19 petagrams of carbon per year per decade (Pg C year −1 decade −1 ) (a mean of 2.8 ± 0.4 Pg C year −1 ), accounting for 35% of fossil emissions between 1990 and 2019. The net land sink shows no robust trend (with a mean of 1.0 ± 0.5 Pg C year −1 , accounting for 13% of fossil emissions), despite large decadal variability. These results challenge many process-based model simulations of the land and ocean sinks, questioning their ability to accurately predict future climate states.

title: ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering drive extracellular vesicle budding from cilia
abstract: Cilia-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate cell-cell communication and remove signaling molecules from cilia. The Hedgehog receptor Smoothened (SMO) is selected for packaging into ciliary EVs by ubiquitin chains, but how cargo selection is coupled to EV budding remains unknown. In this work, working in mouse kidney cells, we found that the ubiquitin reader endosomal sorting complex required for transport–0 (ESCRT-0) orchestrates both cargo selection and EV biogenesis. Unlike the conventional ESCRT pathway, SMO secretion did not require the ESCRT-III membrane scission machinery. Instead, ESCRT-0 condensed at the ciliary tip, where it clustered ubiquitinated SMO to drive EV biogenesis. Disrupting ESCRT-0 condensation blocked SMO secretion, and combining forced recruitment of ESCRT-0 with optogenetic clustering of SMO was sufficient to reconstitute EV budding. Thus, ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering constitute a minimal module for ESCRT-III–independent reverse-topology budding.

title: Early epidemiological and spatial assessment of the Bundibugyo virus outbreak 2026
abstract: A Bundibugyo virus outbreak was first reported on May 15th, 2026 in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with multiple cases reported across health zones during the early phase of the outbreak and suggestions of circulation weeks prior to detection. We pair highly resolved case and testing records with human mobility data to investigate the early outbreak dynamics of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD). We show that human movement was a principle driver of early spatial expansion between May 10th and June 1st when the number of health zones and health areas reporting positive cases increased by 12 and 49, respectively. The early doubling time was estimated at ~10 days. Our work shows the rapid spatial expansion and growth of BVD with implications for intervention strategies.

title: Geodetic observations in West Antarctica reveal geodynamically consistent 3D mantle viscosity
abstract: The rapid ice loss in West Antarctica since the 1990s has led to substantial ice surface lowering, regional bedrock uplift, and gravity reduction, as measured by geodetic observations. The bedrock (crustal) motions and gravity changes result from glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA), a process controlled by Earth’s viscoelastic properties and deglaciation history. In this study, we present GIA models with geodynamically consistent three-dimensional mantle viscoelastic structures and reconstructed ice history for Antarctica from 1900 to 2020, which explain both the observed Global Navigation Satellite System crustal motions and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment gravity changes in West Antarctica. This study demonstrates that a mantle rheology including a weak asthenosphere and temperature-dependent viscosity is consistent with both mantle convection at million-year timescales and ongoing decadal GIA occurring in West Antarctica.

title: Anion Sublattice Engineering Induced Niobium-Tungsten Oxide with Near-Zero Residual Strain for Stable 100 C Cycling Capability
abstract: Abstract Wadsley-Roth W3Nb14O44 is a fast-charging anode material but suffers from low electronic conductivity and electrochemical polarization. Here, anion-sublattice engineering is employed to regulate its electronic structure and Li+ storage kinetics. Density functional theory and kinetic analyses reveal that an appropriate concentration of oxygen vacancies enhances electronic conductivity, moderates Li+ adsorption, and facilitates Li+ diffusion, thereby reducing charge-transfer and diffusion impedances at low temperatures. In situ XRD and synchrotron radiation X-ray 3D nanocomputed tomography reveal reversible structural evolution with near-zero residual strain after cycling. Consequently, WNO-x delivers 77.4 mAh g–1 at 200 C and retains 72.6% capacity after 6000 cycles at 100 C while exhibiting low-temperature electrochemical activity. Moreover, the WNO-x||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 full cell delivers 85.8 mAh g–1 at 20 C and retains 77.1% capacity after 3000 cycles, with cycling capability at –30 °C. Such structure-property insight provides a strategy for designing niobium-based oxide anodes toward fast-charging and low-temperature batteries.
